      "source": "//! 🏷️ Canonical typed value schema and borrowed classification contract.\n\nuse crate::{DslValue, FromValue, ToValue, ValueError};\n\n/// 📐️ One domain-neutral type declaration.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]\npub enum ValueType {\n    Boolean,\n    Integer,\n    Decimal,\n    Text,\n    List(Box<ValueType>),\n    Schema(String),\n    #[default]\n    Any,\n}\n\n/// 🔎️ Classification borrowed from a concrete value owner.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ValueKind<'a> {\n    Null,\n    Boolean,\n    Integer,\n    Decimal,\n    Text,\n    Dictionary(Option<&'a str>),\n}\n\nimpl ValueType {\n    pub fn id(&self) -> String {\n        match self {\n            ValueType::Boolean => \"boolean\".into(),\n            ValueType::Integer => \"integer\".into(),\n            ValueType::Decimal => \"number\".into(),\n            ValueType::Text => \"text\".into(),\n            ValueType::List(_) => \"list\".into(),\n            ValueType::Schema(id) => id.clone(),\n            ValueType::Any => \"value\".into(),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 🎯️ Matches an owner-supplied classification without constructing a value carrier.\n    pub fn matches(&self, value: ValueKind<'_>) -> bool {\n        if value == ValueKind::Null {\n            return false;\n        }\n        match self {\n            ValueType::Any => true,\n            ValueType::Boolean => value == ValueKind::Boolean,\n            ValueType::Integer => value == ValueKind::Integer,\n            ValueType::Decimal => matches!(value, ValueKind::Boolean | ValueKind::Integer | ValueKind::Decimal),\n            ValueType::Text => value == ValueKind::Text,\n            ValueType::List(_) => value == ValueKind::Dictionary(Some(\"list\")),\n            ValueType::Schema(schema) => value == ValueKind::Dictionary(Some(schema)),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl ToValue for ValueType {\n    fn to_value_controlled(&self, control: &mut crate::NativeEncodeControl<'_>) -> Result<DslValue, ValueError> {\n        controlled::encode(self, control)\n    }\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        match self {\n            ValueType::Boolean => DslValue::object([(\"kind\".to_string(), \"boolean\".to_value())]),\n            ValueType::Integer => DslValue::object([(\"kind\".to_string(), \"integer\".to_value())]),\n            ValueType::Decimal => DslValue::object([(\"kind\".to_string(), \"decimal\".to_value())]),\n            ValueType::Text => DslValue::object([(\"kind\".to_string(), \"text\".to_value())]),\n            ValueType::List(inner) => DslValue::object([(\"kind\".to_string(), \"list\".to_value()), (\"of\".to_string(), inner.to_value())]),\n            ValueType::Schema(id) => DslValue::object([(\"kind\".to_string(), \"schema\".to_value()), (\"of\".to_string(), id.to_value())]),\n            ValueType::Any => DslValue::object([(\"kind\".to_string(), \"any\".to_value())]),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl FromValue for ValueType {\n    fn from_value_controlled(value: &DslValue, control: &mut crate::NativeDecodeControl<'_>) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        controlled::decode(value, control)\n    }\n    fn retire_decoded(self) {\n        controlled::retire(self)\n    }\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        let DslValue::Object(fields) = &value else {\n            return Err(ValueError::new(\"expected a type object\"));\n        };\n        let kind = value.get(\"kind\").cloned().map(String::from_value).transpose()?.ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(\"kind\"))?;\n        let expected = if matches!(kind.as_str(), \"list\" | \"schema\") { 2 } else { 1 };\n        if fields.len() != expected || fields.iter().any(|(key, _)| key != \"kind\" && key != \"of\") {\n            return Err(ValueError::new(\"invalid type fields\"));\n        }\n        match kind.as_str() {\n            \"boolean\" => Ok(ValueType::Boolean),\n            \"integer\" => Ok(ValueType::Integer),\n            \"decimal\" => Ok(ValueType::Decimal),\n            \"text\" => Ok(ValueType::Text),\n            \"list\" => Ok(ValueType::List(Box::new(value.get(\"of\").cloned().map(ValueType::from_value).transpose()?.ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(\"of\"))?))),\n            \"schema\" => Ok(ValueType::Schema(value.get(\"of\").cloned().map(String::from_value).transpose()?.ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(\"of\"))?)),\n            \"any\" => Ok(ValueType::Any),\n            other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"unknown ValueType kind '{other}'\"))),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\n#[path = \"🧪️tests/🦀️.rs\"]\nmod tests;\n\n#[path = \"🛬️controlled/🦀️.rs\"]\nmod controlled;\n",

      "source": "//! 🛫️ Borrowed projection into admitted intrinsic native output.\nuse super::{DslValue,ToValue,FromValue,ValueError,NativeEncodeControl,DecodedValue};\n\npub fn scalar(control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<(),ValueError>{control.scoped_stage(|control|{control.begin_stage(1)?;control.step()}).map_err(ValueError::new)}\n\npub fn sequence<'a,T:ToValue+'a>(items:impl ExactSizeIterator<Item=&'a T>,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{\n control.scoped_depth(64,|control|control.scoped_stage(|control|{\n  control.begin_stage(items.len()).map_err(ValueError::new)?;\n  let mut output=Vec::<DslValue>::guard_decoded(control.allocate_vec(items.len()).map_err(ValueError::new)?);\n  for(index,value)in items.enumerate(){output.get_mut().push(value.to_value_controlled(control).map_err(|error|error.under(index))?);control.step().map_err(ValueError::new)?;}\n  Ok(DslValue::Array(output.take()))\n }))\n}\n\npub fn map<'a,K:ToValue+'a,V:ToValue+'a>(items:impl ExactSizeIterator<Item=(&'a K,&'a V)>,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{\n control.scoped_depth(64,|control|control.scoped_stage(|control|{\n  control.begin_stage(items.len()).map_err(ValueError::new)?;\n  let mut output=object(items.len(),control)?;\n  for(key,value)in items{let key=key.to_object_key_controlled(control)?;let child=value.to_value_controlled(control)?;output.get_mut().push((key,child));control.step().map_err(ValueError::new)?;}\n  Ok(DslValue::Object(output.take()))\n }))\n}\n\npub fn object(count:usize,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DecodedValue<Vec<(String,DslValue)>>,ValueError>{Ok(DecodedValue::new(control.allocate_vec(count).map_err(ValueError::new)?,|items|{for(_,value)in items{super::controlled::retire_intrinsic(value)}}))}\n\nstruct StackText{bytes:[u8;4096],length:usize}\nimpl std::fmt::Write for StackText{fn write_str(&mut self,text:&str)->std::fmt::Result{let end=self.length.checked_add(text.len()).filter(|end|*end<=self.bytes.len()).ok_or(std::fmt::Error)?;self.bytes[self.length..end].copy_from_slice(text.as_bytes());self.length=end;Ok(())}}\nimpl StackText{fn new()->Self{Self{bytes:[0;4096],length:0}}fn text(&self)->&str{std::str::from_utf8(&self.bytes[..self.length]).expect(\"formatted UTF-8\")}}\n\npub fn key(value:impl std::fmt::Display,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<String,ValueError>{use std::fmt::Write;let mut text=StackText::new();control.checkpoint().map_err(ValueError::new)?;write!(text,\"{value}\").map_err(|_|ValueError::new(\"native numeric key exceeds bounded formatting\"))?;control.copy_text(text.text()).map_err(ValueError::new)}\n\npub fn float32(value:f32,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{\n use std::fmt::Write;scalar(control)?;let bits=value.to_bits();let payload=bits&0x007f_ffff;\n if bits&0x7f80_0000==0x7f80_0000&&payload!=0{return Ok(DslValue::Number(super::Number::Float(f64::from_bits((u64::from(bits&0x8000_0000)<<32)|0x7ff0_0000_0000_0000|(u64::from(payload)<<29)))))}\n let mut shortest=StackText::new();write!(shortest,\"{value:e}\").map_err(|_|ValueError::new(\"native float formatting overflow\"))?;let precision=shortest.text().split('e').next().unwrap().bytes().filter(u8::is_ascii_digit).count().saturating_sub(1);let mut exact=StackText::new();write!(exact,\"{value:.precision$e}\").map_err(|_|ValueError::new(\"native float formatting overflow\"))?;Ok(DslValue::Number(super::Number::Float(exact.text().parse().map_err(|_|ValueError::new(\"native float formatting failed\"))?)))\n}\n\nfn push<T>(values:&mut Vec<T>,value:T,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<(),(ValueError,T)>{\n    if values.len()==values.capacity(){\n        let next=values.capacity().max(1).checked_mul(2).and_then(|n|n.checked_mul(size_of::<T>())).filter(|bytes|*bytes<=isize::MAX as usize);\n        let Some(bytes)=next else{return Err((ValueError::new(\"native frontier size overflow\"),value))};\n        if let Err(error)=control.charge(bytes){return Err((ValueError::new(error),value))}\n        if values.try_reserve_exact(values.capacity().max(1)).is_err(){return Err((ValueError::new(\"native frontier allocation failed\"),value))}\n    }\n    values.push(value);Ok(())\n}\n\nenum Task<'a>{Value(&'a DslValue),Array(usize),Object(&'a[(String,DslValue)])}\n\npub fn intrinsic(value:&DslValue,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{\n    match value{\n     DslValue::Null=>{scalar(control)?;return Ok(DslValue::Null)},DslValue::Bool(value)=>{scalar(control)?;return Ok(DslValue::Bool(*value))},DslValue::Number(value)=>{scalar(control)?;return Ok(DslValue::Number(*value))},DslValue::String(value)=>return control.copy_text(value).map(DslValue::String).map_err(ValueError::new),DslValue::Bytes(value)=>return control.copy_bytes(value).map(DslValue::Bytes).map_err(ValueError::new),DslValue::Array(_)|DslValue::Object(_)=>{}\n    }\n    control.scoped_stage(|control|{\n Retires an admitted child if its parent cannot publish a complete owner.\npub struct DecodedValue<T> { value:Option<T>, retire:fn(T) }\nimpl<T> DecodedValue<T> {\n    pub fn new(value:T,retire:fn(T))->Self{Self{value:Some(value),retire}}\n    pub fn get(&self)->&T{self.value.as_ref().expect(\"owned value present\")}\n    pub fn get_mut(&mut self)->&mut T{self.value.as_mut().expect(\"owned value present\")}\n    pub fn take(mut self)->T{self.value.take().expect(\"owned value present\")}\n}\nimpl<T> Drop for DecodedValue<T>{fn drop(&mut self){if let Some(value)=self.value.take(){(self.retire)(value)}}}\n\npub fn scalar(control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<(),ValueError>{control.scoped_stage(|control|{control.begin_stage(1)?;control.step()}).map_err(ValueError::new)}\n\npub fn sequence<T:FromValue>(value:&DslValue,control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Vec<T>,ValueError>{\n    let DslValue::Array(items)=value else{return Err(ValueError::new(\"expected array\"))};\n    control.scoped_stage(|control|{\n        control.begin_stage(items.len()).map_err(ValueError::new)?;\n        let mut output=Vec::<T>::guard_decoded(control.allocate_vec(items.len()).map_err(ValueError::new)?);\n        for(index,value)in items.iter().enumerate(){let child=T::from_value_controlled(value,control).map_err(|e|e.under(index))?;output.get_mut().push(child);control.step().map_err(ValueError::new)?;}\n        Ok(output.take())\n    })\n}\n\npub fn set<T:FromValue+Ord>(value:&DslValue,control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<std::collections::BTreeSet<T>,ValueError>{\n    let DslValue::Array(items)=value else{return Err(ValueError::new(\"expected array\"))};\n    control.scoped_stage(|control|{\n        control.begin_stage(items.len()).map_err(ValueError::new)?;\n        let mut output=std::collections::BTreeSet::<T>::new().guard_decoded();\n        for(index,value)in items.iter().enumerate(){\n            control.charge(tree_allocation::<T>(output.get().len()).ok_or_else(||ValueError::new(\"set allocation overflow\"))?).map_err(ValueError::new)?;\n            let child=T::from_value_controlled(value,control).map_err(|e|e.under(index))?.guard_decoded();\n            if !output.get().contains(child.get()){output.get_mut().insert(child.take());}\n            control.step().map_err(ValueError::new)?;\n        }\n        Ok(output.take())\n    })\n}\n\npub fn hash_set<T:FromValue+Eq+std::hash::Hash,S:ControlledValueHasher>(value:&DslValue,control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<std::collections::HashSet<T,S>,ValueError>{\n    let DslValue::Array(items)=value else{return Err(ValueError::new(\"expected array\"))};\n    control.scoped_stage(|control|{\n        control.begin_stage(items.len()).map_err(ValueError::new)?;\n        control.charge(hash_allocation::<T>(items.len()).ok_or_else(||ValueError::new(\"hash set allocation overflow\"))?).map_err(ValueError::new)?;\n        let mut set=std::collections::HashSet::<T,S>::with_hasher(S::from_value_controlled(control)?);\n        set.try_reserve(items.len()).map_err(|_|ValueError::new(\"hash set allocation failed\"))?;\n        let mut output=set.guard_decoded();\n        for(index,value)in items.iter().enumerate(){\n            let child=T::from_value_controlled(value,control).map_err(|error|error.under(index))?.guard_decoded();\n            if !output.get().contains(child.get()){output.get_mut().insert(child.take());}\n            control.step().map_err(ValueError::new)?;\n        }\n        Ok(output.take())\n    })\n}\n\npub fn map<T:FromValue>(value:&DslValue,control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<std::collections::BTreeMap<String,T>,ValueError>{\n    let DslValue::Object(entries)=value else{return Err(ValueError::new(\"expected object\"))};\n    control.scoped_stage(|control|{\n        control.begin_stage(entries.len()).map_err(ValueError::new)?;\n        let mut output=std::collections::BTreeMap::<String,T>::new().guard_decoded();\n        for(index,(key,value))in entries.iter().enumerate(){\n            control.charge(tree_allocation::<(String,T)>(output.get().len()).ok_or_else(||ValueError::new(\"map allocation       "source": "//! 🔁️ `ToValue`/`FromValue` — the first-party analog of `serde::Serialize`/\n//! `serde::de::DeserializeOwned`, over [`super::DslValue`] instead of a generic visitor.\n//!\n//! Exists to break the forced `serde` dependency `MutationDiff`/`Mutation` (`crate::mutation`)\n//! used to bake into every implementor: those traits now bound on `ToValue + FromValue`, so a\n//! plugin implementing them never needs to depend on `serde`. See\n//! `.🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️09/☀️01/RUNTIME-DEPENDENCY-ELIMINATION-FOR-S-PLUGINS-AND-ARTIFACTS/\n//! 🔍️research/📓️serde-replacement-surface.md` for the design rationale and the older\n//! `super::dsl_value_serde` bridge this supersedes for plugin-facing code (that bridge itself\n//! requires `serde::Serialize`/`serde::de::DeserializeOwned` on its input, so it cannot be the\n//! plugin-facing seam — it stays only for framework-internal callers that still speak serde).\n//!\n//! `#[derive(ToValue, FromValue)]` (`semio-framework-value-derive`, `🌱️value/✨️derive`) implements\n//! both traits for a `#[value(...)]`-annotated struct/enum; the scalar/container leaves below are\n//! the hand-written base cases every derived impl bottoms out on.\n\nuse super::{DslValue, Number};\nuse super::native_decoding::NativeDecodeControl;\nuse super::native_encoding::NativeEncodeControl;\n#[path=\"🛬️controlled/🦀️.rs\"]\nmod controlled;\npub use controlled::DecodedValue;\n#[path=\"🛫️controlled/🦀️.rs\"]\nmod encoding;\n\n/// 🔑️ A hash-builder owner admits its own default state before controlled collection construction.\npub trait ControlledValueHasher: std::hash::BuildHasher + Default {\n    fn from_value_controlled(control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError> where Self:Sized;\n}\nimpl ControlledValueHasher for std::collections::hash_map::RandomState {\n    fn from_value_controlled(control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(control)?;Ok(Self::new())}\n}\n\n//#region 🔖️Traits\n/// 🔁️ Converts `self` into a [`DslValue`] tree. First-party analog of `serde::Serialize`.\npub trait ToValue {\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue;\n\n    /// 🛫️ Constructs owned native output through an explicit cumulative allocation control.\n    fn to_value_controlled(&self,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{control.checkpoint().map_err(ValueError::new)?;Err(ValueError::new(\"value owner has no controlled native encoding implementation\"))}\n\n    /// 🔑️ Formats one owned map key without an uncontrolled `ToString` allocation.\n    fn to_object_key_controlled(&self,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<String,ValueError>{control.checkpoint().map_err(ValueError::new)?;Err(ValueError::new(\"value key owner has no controlled native encoding implementation\"))}\n\n\n    fn value_at_path(&self, path: &[&str]) -> Result<DslValue, ValueError> {\n        self.to_value().value_at_path(path)\n    }\n\n    fn value_shape_at_path(&self, path: &[&str]) -> Result<ValueShape, ValueError> {\n        Ok(ValueShape::of(&self.value_at_path(path)?))\n    }\n\n    fn value_key_at_path(&self, path: &[&str], index: usize) -> Result<String, ValueError> {\n        match self.value_at_path(path)? {\n            DslValue::Object(entries) => entries.get(index).map(|(key, _)| key.clone()).ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(format!(\"object key index {index} is out of range for length {}\", entries.len()))),\n            other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected an object, found {other:?}\"))),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🔁️ Hydrates `Self` from a [`DslValue`] tree. First-party analog of\n/// `serde::de::DeserializeOwned`.\npub trait FromValue: Sized {\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError>;\n\n    /// 🛬️ Constructs from borrowed native state under one cumulative ownership control.\n    fn from_value_controlled(_value: &DslValue, control: &mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        control.checkpoint().map_err(ValueError::new)?;\n        Err(ValueError::new(\"value owner has no controlled native construction implementation\"))\n    }\n\n    /// 🔑️ Constructs a typed object key without an uncontrolled `FromStr` allocation.\n    fn from_object_key_controlled(_key:&str,control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{\n        control.checkpoint().map_err(ValueError::new)?;Err(ValueError::new(\"value key owner has no controlled construction implementation\"))\n    }\n\n    /// 🌱️ Admits a missing field's default without invoking an uncontrolled allocator.\n    fn default_value_controlled(control: &mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        control.checkpoint().map_err(ValueError::new)?;\n        Err(ValueError::new(\"value owner has no controlled default construction implementation\"))\n    }\n\n    /// 🛡️ Holds a completed child until its parent can publish a complete value.\n    fn guard_decoded(self) -> DecodedValue<Self> { DecodedValue::new(self, Self::retire_decoded) }\n\n    /// ♻️ Retires a completed child when a later construction step fails.\n    fn retire_decoded(self) { drop(self); }\n\n\n    fn edit_value_at_path(&mut self, path: &[&str], edit: ValueEdit) -> Result<(), ValueError> {\n        if !path.is_empty() {\n            return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"value has no child `{}`\", path[0])));\n        }\n        match edit {\n            ValueEdit::Set(value) => {\n                *self = <Self as FromValue>::from_value(value)?;\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            ValueEdit::Insert(_) | ValueEdit::InsertAt { .. } => Err(ValueError::new(\"cannot insert at the value root\")),\n            ValueEdit::Remove => Err(ValueError::new(\"cannot remove the value root\")),\n        }\n    }\n\n}\n\n/// ✏️ One structural edit over already-decoded value path segments.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]\npub enum ValueEdit {\n    Set(DslValue),\n    Insert(DslValue),\n    /// 🗂️ Places an ordered object member; intrinsically ordered maps retain their key semantics.\n    InsertAt { index: usize, value: DslValue },\n    Remove,\n}\n\n/// 📐 Describes a value at a typed path without materializing its children.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ValueShape {\n    Null,\n    Bool,\n    Number,\n    String,\n    Bytes { len: usize },\n    Array { len: usize },\n    Object { len: usize },\n}\n\nimpl ValueShape {\n    pub fn of(value: &DslValue) -> Self {\n        match value {\n            DslValue::Null => Self::Null,\n            DslValue::Bool(_) => Self::Bool,\n            DslValue::Number(_) => Self::Number,\n            DslValue::String(_) => Self::String,\n            DslValue::Bytes(bytes) => Self::Bytes{len:bytes.len()},\n            DslValue::Array(items) => Self::Array { len: items.len() },\n            DslValue::Object(entries) => Self::Object { len: entries.len() },\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🚨️ A decode failure, with a dotted field/index/variant path prefixed as the caller\n/// unwinds (see [`ValueError::under`]) so a nested failure reads as `\"steps.3.title: ...\"`.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ValueError(pub String);\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ValueError {\n    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        formatter.write_str(&self.0)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for ValueError {}\nimpl From<String> for ValueError { fn from(message:String)->Self{Self(message)} }\n\nimpl ValueError {\n    pub fn new(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        Self(message.into())\n    }\n\n    /// 🪆️ Prefixes one outer path segment (a field name, array index, or enum variant) onto an\n    /// inner decode failure — called bottom-up as `from_value` unwinds a nested struct/array.\n    pub fn under(self, segment: impl std::fmt::Display) -> Self {\n        Self(format!(\"{segment}.{}\", self.0))\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🧭️ Applies `edit` at `path` of a value whose codec is hand-written: through the value tree the codec emits, decoded back\n/// so every invariant its `from_value` checks holds for the edited value — the path edit a derived [`FromValue`] performs\n/// field by field. On failure `target` is unchanged. A hand-written `FromValue` routes its `edit_value_at_path` here.\npub fn edit_through_value<T: ToValue + FromValue>(target: &mut T, path: &[&str], edit: ValueEdit) -> Result<(), ValueError> {\n    let mut value = target.to_value();\n    value.edit_value_at_path(path, edit)?;\n    *target = T::from_value(value)?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn path_index(segment: &str, length: usize, insert: bool) -> Result<usize, ValueError> {\n    if insert && segment == \"-\" {\n        return Ok(length);\n    }\n    if segment.is_empty() || (segment.len() > 1 && segment.starts_with('0')) || !segment.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit()) {\n        return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"invalid canonical array index `{segment}`\")));\n    }\n    let index = segment.parse::<usize>().map_err(|_| ValueError::new(format!(\"array index `{segment}` is out of range\")))?;\n    let admitted = if insert { index <= length } else { index < length };\n    admitted.then_some(index).ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(format!(\"array index `{segment}` is out of range for length {length}\")))\n}\n\nfn object_entry_index(entries: &[(String, DslValue)], key: &str) -> Result<Option<usize>, ValueError> {\n    let mut matches = entries.iter().enumerate().filter(|(_, (candidate, _))| candidate == key).map(|(index, _)| index);\n    let first = matches.next();\n    if matches.next().is_some() {\n        return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"duplicate object key `{key}`\")));\n    }\n    Ok(first)\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️Traits\n\n//#region 🔖️Scalars\n/// 🔢️ Unsigned integer scalars — round-trip through [`Number::UInt`] so a wire-visible\n/// `u64` field (e.g. `ttl_secs`) encodes as bare `3600`, never `3600.0`. See\n/// `.🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️09/☀️01/RUNTIME-DEPENDENCY-ELIMINATION-FOR-S-PLUGINS-AND-ARTIFACTS/\n/// 🔍️research/📓️dslvalue-integer-fidelity.md`.\nmacro_rules! impl_uint_codec {\n    ($($ty:ty),+ $(,)?) => {\n        $(\n            impl ToValue for $ty {\n                fn to_value_controlled(&self,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{encoding::scalar(control)?;Ok(DslValue::Number(Number::UInt(*self as u64)))}\n                fn to_object_key_controlled(&self,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<String,ValueError>{encoding::key(*self,control)}\n                fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n                    DslValue::Number(Number::UInt(*self as u64))\n                }\n            }\n            impl FromValue for $ty {\n                fn from_object_key_controlled(key:&str,control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(control)?;key.parse().map_err(|_|ValueError::new(\"invalid numeric object key\"))}\n\n                fn from_value_controlled(value:&DslValue,control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{\n                    controlled::scalar(control)?;match value{DslValue::Number(number)=>number.as_u64().and_then(|n| <$ty>::try_from(n).ok()).ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(\"expected exact unsigned integer\")),_=>Err(ValueError::new(\"expected number\"))}\n                }\n                fn default_value_controlled(control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(control)?;Ok(0 as $ty)}\n\n                fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n                    match value {\n                        DslValue::Number(number) => number.as_u64().and_then(|n| <$ty>::try_from(n).ok())\n                            .ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(format!(\"expected an exact {} integer, found {number:?}\", stringify!($ty)))),\n                        other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a number, found {other:?}\"))),\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        )+\n    };\n}\nimpl_uint_codec!(u8, u16, u32, u64, usize);\n\n/// 🔢️ Signed integer scalars — round-trip through [`Number::Int`], same fidelity contract as the\n/// unsigned family above.\nmacro_rules! impl_int_codec {\n    ($($ty:ty),+ $(,)?) => {\n        $(\n            impl ToValue for $ty {\n                fn to_value_controlled(&self,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{encoding::scalar(control)?;Ok(DslValue::Number(Number::Int(*self as i64)))}\n                fn to_object_key_controlled(&self,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<String,ValueError>{encoding::key(*self,control)}\n                fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n                    DslValue::Number(Number::Int(*self as i64))\n                }\n            }\n            impl FromValue for $ty {\n                fn from_object_key_controlled(key:&str,control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(control)?;key.parse().map_err(|_|ValueError::new(\"invalid numeric object key\"))}\n\n                fn from_value_controlled(value:&DslValue,control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{\n                    controlled::scalar(control)?;match value{DslValue::Number(number)=>number.as_i64().and_then(|n| <$ty>::try_from(n).ok()).ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(\"expected exact signed integer\")),_=>Err(ValueError::new(\"expected number\"))}\n                }\n                fn default_value_controlled(control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(control)?;Ok(0 as $ty)}\n\n                fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n                    match value {\n                        DslValue::Number(number) => number.as_i64().and_then(|n| <$ty>::try_from(n).ok())\n                            .ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(format!(\"expected an exact {} integer, found {number:?}\", stringify!($ty)))),\n                        other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a number, found {other:?}\"))),\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        )+\n    };\n}\nimpl_int_codec!(i8, i16, i32, i64, isize);\n\n/// 🔢️ Fractional scalars — always encode/decode through [`Number::Float`]; a whole float keeps its\n/// explicit `.0` on the wire so it never collapses onto its integer twin.\nmacro_rules! impl_float_codec {\n    ($($ty:ty),+ $(,)?) => {\n        $(\n            impl ToValue for $ty {\n                fn to_value_controlled(&self,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{encoding::scalar(control)?;Ok(DslValue::Number(Number::Float(*self as f64)))}\n                fn to_object_key_controlled(&self,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<String,ValueError>{encoding::key(*self,control)}\n                fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n                    DslValue::Number(Number::Float(*self as f64))\n                }\n            }\n            impl FromValue for $ty {\n                fn from_object_key_controlled(key:&str,control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(control)?;key.parse().map_err(|_|ValueError::new(\"invalid numeric object key\"))}\n\n                fn from_value_controlled(value:&DslValue,control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{\n                    controlled::scalar(control)?;match value{DslValue::Number(number)=>Ok(number.as_f64() as $ty),_=>Err(ValueError::new(\"expected number\"))}\n                }\n                fn default_value_controlled(control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(control)?;Ok(0 as $ty)}\n\n                fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n                    match value {\n                        DslValue::Number(n) => Ok(n.as_f64() as $ty),\n                        other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a number, found {other:?}\"))),\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        )+\n    };\n}\nimpl_float_codec!(f64);\n\nfn float32_from_number(number:Number)->f32{\n    let value=number.as_f64();let bits=value.to_bits();let payload=bits&0x000f_ffff_ffff_ffff;\n    if bits&0x7ff0_0000_0000_0000==0x7ff0_0000_0000_0000&&payload!=0{f32::from_bits(((bits>>32) as u32&0x8000_0000)|0x7f80_0000|((payload>>29) as u32).max(1))}else{value as f32}\n}\n\nimpl ToValue for f32 {\nfn to_value_controlled(&self,c:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{encoding::float32(*self,c)}\nfn to_object_key_controlled(&self,c:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<String,ValueError>{encoding::key(*self,c)}\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        let bits=self.to_bits();let payload=bits&0x007f_ffff;\n        if bits&0x7f80_0000==0x7f80_0000&&payload!=0{return DslValue::Number(Number::Float(f64::from_bits((u64::from(bits&0x8000_0000)<<32)|0x7ff0_0000_0000_0000|(u64::from(payload)<<29))))}\n        let shortest = format!(\"{self:e}\");\n        let precision = shortest.split('e').next().unwrap().bytes().filter(u8::is_ascii_digit).count().saturating_sub(1);\n        DslValue::Number(Number::Float(format!(\"{self:.precision$e}\").parse().expect(\"f32 decimal text is a valid f64\")))\n    }\n}\n\nimpl FromValue for f32 {\nfn from_value_controlled(value:&DslValue,c:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(c)?;match value{DslValue::Number(n)=>Ok(float32_from_number(*n)),_=>Err(ValueError::new(\"expected number\"))}}\nfn default_value_controlled(c:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(c)?;Ok(0.0)}\n\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        match value {\n            DslValue::Number(number) => Ok(float32_from_number(number)),\n            other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a number, found {other:?}\"))),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl ToValue for bool {\nfn to_value_controlled(&self,c:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{encoding::scalar(c)?;Ok(DslValue::Bool(*self))}\nfn to_object_key_controlled(&self,c:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<String,ValueError>{encoding::key(*self,c)}\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        DslValue::Bool(*self)\n    }\n}\nimpl FromValue for bool {\nfn from_object_key_controlled(key:&str,control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(control)?;key.parse().map_err(|_|ValueError::new(\"invalid boolean object key\"))}\n\nfn from_value_controlled(v:&DslValue,c:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(c)?;match v{DslValue::Bool(v)=>Ok(*v),_=>Err(ValueError::new(\"expected bool\"))}}\nfn default_value_controlled(c:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(c)?;Ok(false)}\n\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        match value {\n            DslValue::Bool(b) => Ok(b),\n            other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a bool, found {other:?}\"))),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl ToValue for String {\nfn to_value_controlled(&self,c:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{c.copy_text(self).map(DslValue::String).map_err(ValueError::new)}\nfn to_object_key_controlled(&self,c:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<String,ValueError>{c.copy_text(self).map_err(ValueError::new)}\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        DslValue::String(self.clone())\n    }\n}\nimpl FromValue for String {\nfn from_object_key_controlled(key:&str,control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(control)?;control.copy_text(key).map_err(ValueError::new)}\n\nfn from_value_controlled(v:&DslValue,c:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(c)?;match v{DslValue::String(v)=>c.copy_text(v).map_err(ValueError::new),_=>Err(ValueError::new(\"expected string\"))}}\nfn default_value_controlled(c:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(c)?;Ok(String::new())}\n\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        match value {\n            DslValue::String(s) => Ok(s),\n            other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a string, found {other:?}\"))),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🗂️ A path renders as its UTF-8 string form (lossy on the encode side — this is a local-only\n/// config value, never a content-addressed hash input, so exact non-Unicode byte round-tripping\n/// is not required the way `serde`'s own `Path`/`PathBuf` impl demands it).\nimpl ToValue for std::path::PathBuf {\nfn to_value_controlled(&self,c:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{encoding::path(self,c)}\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        DslValue::String(self.to_string_lossy().into_owned())\n    }\n}\nimpl FromValue for std::path::PathBuf {\nfn from_value_controlled(v:&DslValue,c:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{String::from_value_controlled(v,c).map(Self::from)}\nfn default_value_controlled(c:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(c)?;Ok(Self::new())}\n\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        match value {\n            DslValue::String(s) => Ok(std::path::PathBuf::from(s)),\n            other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a string, found {other:?}\"))),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🌉️ No `FromValue` counterpart — decoding always needs owned data, `String`'s impl covers it.\nimpl ToValue for &str {\nfn to_value_controlled(&self,c:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{c.copy_text(self).map(DslValue::String).map_err(ValueError::new)}\nfn to_object_key_controlled(&self,c:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<String,ValueError>{c.copy_text(self).map_err(ValueError::new)}\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        DslValue::String(self.to_string())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl ToValue for () {\nfn to_value_controlled(&self,c:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{encoding::scalar(c)?;Ok(DslValue::Null)}\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        DslValue::Null\n    }\n}\nimpl FromValue for () {\nfn from_value_controlled(v:&DslValue,c:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(c)?;match v{DslValue::Null=>Ok(()),_=>Err(ValueError::new(\"expected null\"))}}\nfn default_value_controlled(c:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(c)}\n\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        match value {\n            DslValue::Null => Ok(()),\n            other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected null, found {other:?}\"))),\n        }\n    }\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️Scalars\n\n//#region 🔖️Containers\nimpl<T: ToValue> ToValue for Option<T> {\nfn to_value_controlled(&self,c:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{c.scoped_depth(64,|c|match self{Some(value)=>value.to_value_controlled(c),None=>().to_value_controlled(c)})}\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        match self {\n            Some(value) => value.to_value(),\n            None => DslValue::Null,\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn value_at_path(&self, path: &[&str]) -> Result<DslValue, ValueError> {\n        match (path.is_empty(), self) {\n            (true, _) => Ok(self.to_value()),\n            (false, Some(value)) => value.value_at_path(path),\n            (false, None) => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"null has no child `{}`\", path[0]))),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn value_shape_at_path(&self, path: &[&str]) -> Result<ValueShape, ValueError> {\n        match (path.is_empty(), self) {\n            (true, None) => Ok(ValueShape::Null),\n            (true, Some(value)) => value.value_shape_at_path(path),\n            (false, Some(value)) => value.value_shape_at_path(path),\n            (false, None) => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"null has no child `{}`\", path[0]))),\n        }\n    }\n\n    fn value_key_at_path(&self, path: &[&str], index: usize) -> Result<String, ValueError> {\n        self.as_ref().ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(\"expected an object, found null\"))?.value_key_at_path(path, index)\n    }\n}\nimpl<T: FromValue> FromValue for Option<T> {\nfn from_value_controlled(v:&DslValue,c:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{match v{DslValue::Null=>{controlled::scalar(c)?;Ok(None)},v=>T::from_value_controlled(v,c).map(Some)}}\nfn default_value_controlled(c:&mut         "source": "//! 🔁️ `ToValue`/`FromValue` — the first-party analog of `serde::Serialize`/\n//! `serde::de::DeserializeOwned`, over [`super::DslValue`] instead of a generic visitor.\n//!\n//! Exists to break the forced `serde` dependency `MutationDiff`/`Mutation` (`crate::mutation`)\n//! used to bake into every implementor: those traits now bound on `ToValue + FromValue`, so a\n//! plugin implementing them never needs to depend on `serde`. See\n//! `.🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️09/☀️01/RUNTIME-DEPENDENCY-ELIMINATION-FOR-S-PLUGINS-AND-ARTIFACTS/\n//! 🔍️research/📓️serde-replacement-surface.md` for the design rationale and the older\n//! `super::dsl_value_serde` bridge this supersedes for plugin-facing code (that bridge itself\n//! requires `serde::Serialize`/`serde::de::DeserializeOwned` on its input, so it cannot be the\n//! plugin-facing seam — it stays only for framework-internal callers that still speak serde).\n//!\n//! `#[derive(ToValue, FromValue)]` (`semio-framework-value-derive`, `🌱️value/✨️derive`) implements\n//! both traits for a `#[value(...)]`-annotated struct/enum; the scalar/container leaves below are\n//! the hand-written base cases every derived impl bottoms out on.\n\nuse super::{DslValue, Number};\nuse super::native_decoding::NativeDecodeControl;\nuse super::native_encoding::NativeEncodeControl;\n#[path=\"🛬️controlled/🦀️.rs\"]\nmod controlled;\npub use controlled::DecodedValue;\n#[path=\"🛫️controlled/🦀️.rs\"]\nmod encoding;\n\n/// 🔑️ A hash-builder owner admits its own default state before controlled collection construction.\npub trait ControlledValueHasher: std::hash::BuildHasher + Default {\n    fn from_value_controlled(control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError> where Self:Sized;\n}\nimpl ControlledValueHasher for std::collections::hash_map::RandomState {\n    fn from_value_controlled(control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(control)?;Ok(Self::new())}\n}\n\n//#region 🔖️Traits\n/// 🔁️ Converts `self` into a [`DslValue`] tree. First-party analog of `serde::Serialize`.\npub trait ToValue {\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue;\n\n    /// 🛫️ Constructs owned native output through an explicit cumulative allocation control.\n    fn to_value_controlled(&self,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{control.checkpoint().map_err(ValueError::new)?;Err(ValueError::new(\"value owner has no controlled native encoding implementation\"))}\n\n    /// 🔑️ Formats one owned map key without an uncontrolled `ToString` allocation.\n    fn to_object_key_controlled(&self,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<String,ValueError>{control.checkpoint().map_err(ValueError::new)?;Err(ValueError::new(\"value key owner has no controlled native encoding implementation\"))}\n\n\n    fn value_at_path(&self, path: &[&str]) -> Result<DslValue, ValueError> {\n        self.to_value().value_at_path(path)\n    }\n\n    fn value_shape_at_path(&self, path: &[&str]) -> Result<ValueShape, ValueError> {\n        Ok(ValueShape::of(&self.value_at_path(path)?))\n    }\n\n    fn value_key_at_path(&self, path: &[&str], index: usize) -> Result<String, ValueError> {\n        match self.value_at_path(path)? {\n            DslValue::Object(entries) => entries.get(index).map(|(key, _)| key.clone()).ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(format!(\"object key index {index} is out of range for length {}\", entries.len()))),\n            other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected an object, found {other:?}\"))),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🔁️ Hydrates `Self` from a [`DslValue`] tree. First-party analog of\n/// `serde::de::DeserializeOwned`.\npub trait FromValue: Sized {\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError>;\n\n    /// 🛬️ Constructs from borrowed native state under one cumulative ownership control.\n    fn from_value_controlled(_value: &DslValue, control: &mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        control.checkpoint().map_err(ValueError::new)?;\n        Err(ValueError::new(\"value owner has no controlled native construction implementation\"))\n    }\n\n    /// 🔑️ Constructs a typed object key without an uncontrolled `FromStr` allocation.\n    fn from_object_key_controlled(_key:&str,control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{\n        control.checkpoint().map_err(ValueError::new)?;Err(ValueError::new(\"value key owner has no controlled construction implementation\"))\n    }\n\n    /// 🌱️ Admits a missing field's default without invoking an uncontrolled allocator.\n    fn default_value_controlled(control: &mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        control.checkpoint().map_err(ValueError::new)?;\n        Err(ValueError::new(\"value owner has no controlled default construction implementation\"))\n    }\n\n    /// 🛡️ Holds a completed child until its parent can publish a complete value.\n    fn guard_decoded(self) -> DecodedValue<Self> { DecodedValue::new(self, Self::retire_decoded) }\n\n    /// ♻️ Retires a completed child when a later construction step fails.\n    fn retire_decoded(self) { drop(self); }\n\n\n    fn edit_value_at_path(&mut self, path: &[&str], edit: ValueEdit) -> Result<(), ValueError> {\n        if !path.is_empty() {\n            return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"value has no child `{}`\", path[0])));\n        }\n        match edit {\n            ValueEdit::Set(value) => {\n                *self = <Self as FromValue>::from_value(value)?;\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            ValueEdit::Insert(_) | ValueEdit::InsertAt { .. } => Err(ValueError::new(\"cannot insert at the value root\")),\n            ValueEdit::Remove => Err(ValueError::new(\"cannot remove the value root\")),\n        }\n    }\n\n}\n\n/// ✏️ One structural edit over already-decoded value path segments.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]\npub enum ValueEdit {\n    Set(DslValue),\n    Insert(DslValue),\n    /// 🗂️ Places an ordered object member; intrinsically ordered maps retain their key semantics.\n    InsertAt { index: usize, value: DslValue },\n    Remove,\n}\n\n/// 📐 Describes a value at a typed path without materializing its children.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum ValueShape {\n    Null,\n    Bool,\n    Number,\n    String,\n    Bytes { len: usize },\n    Array { len: usize },\n    Object { len: usize },\n}\n\nimpl ValueShape {\n    pub fn of(value: &DslValue) -> Self {\n        match value {\n            DslValue::Null => Self::Null,\n            DslValue::Bool(_) => Self::Bool,\n            DslValue::Number(_) => Self::Number,\n            DslValue::String(_) => Self::String,\n            DslValue::Bytes(bytes) => Self::Bytes{len:bytes.len()},\n            DslValue::Array(items) => Self::Array { len: items.len() },\n            DslValue::Object(entries) => Self::Object { len: entries.len() },\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🚨️ A decode failure, with a dotted field/index/variant path prefixed as the caller\n/// unwinds (see [`ValueError::under`]) so a nested failure reads as `\"steps.3.title: ...\"`.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct ValueError(pub String);\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for ValueError {\n    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        formatter.write_str(&self.0)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for ValueError {}\nimpl From<String> for ValueError { fn from(message:String)->Self{Self(message)} }\n\nimpl ValueError {\n    pub fn new(message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        Self(message.into())\n    }\n\n    /// 🪆️ Prefixes one outer path segment (a field name, array index, or enum variant) onto an\n    /// inner decode failure — called bottom-up as `from_value` unwinds a nested struct/array.\n    pub fn under(self, segment: impl std::fmt::Display) -> Self {\n        Self(format!(\"{segment}.{}\", self.0))\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🧭️ Applies `edit` at `path` of a value whose codec is hand-written: through the value tree the codec emits, decoded back\n/// so every invariant its `from_value` checks holds for the edited value — the path edit a derived [`FromValue`] performs\n/// field by field. On failure `target` is unchanged. A hand-written `FromValue` routes its `edit_value_at_path` here.\npub fn edit_through_value<T: ToValue + FromValue>(target: &mut T, path: &[&str], edit: ValueEdit) -> Result<(), ValueError> {\n    let mut value = target.to_value();\n    value.edit_value_at_path(path, edit)?;\n    *target = T::from_value(value)?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn path_index(segment: &str, length: usize, insert: bool) -> Result<usize, ValueError> {\n    if insert && segment == \"-\" {\n        return Ok(length);\n    }\n    if segment.is_empty() || (segment.len() > 1 && segment.starts_with('0')) || !segment.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit()) {\n        return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"invalid canonical array index `{segment}`\")));\n    }\n    let index = segment.parse::<usize>().map_err(|_| ValueError::new(format!(\"array index `{segment}` is out of range\")))?;\n    let admitted = if insert { index <= length } else { index < length };\n    admitted.then_some(index).ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(format!(\"array index `{segment}` is out of range for length {length}\")))\n}\n\nfn object_entry_index(entries: &[(String, DslValue)], key: &str) -> Result<Option<usize>, ValueError> {\n    let mut matches = entries.iter().enumerate().filter(|(_, (candidate, _))| candidate == key).map(|(index, _)| index);\n    let first = matches.next();\n    if matches.next().is_some() {\n        return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"duplicate object key `{key}`\")));\n    }\n    Ok(first)\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️Traits\n\n//#region 🔖️Scalars\n/// 🔢️ Unsigned integer scalars — round-trip through [`Number::UInt`] so a wire-visible\n/// `u64` field (e.g. `ttl_secs`) encodes as bare `3600`, never `3600.0`. See\n/// `.🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️09/☀️01/RUNTIME-DEPENDENCY-ELIMINATION-FOR-S-PLUGINS-AND-ARTIFACTS/\n/// 🔍️research/📓️dslvalue-integer-fidelity.md`.\nmacro_rules! impl_uint_codec {\n    ($($ty:ty),+ $(,)?) => {\n        $(\n            impl ToValue for $ty {\n                fn to_value_controlled(&self,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{encoding::scalar(control)?;Ok(DslValue::Number(Number::UInt(*self as u64)))}\n                fn to_object_key_controlled(&self,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<String,ValueError>{encoding::key(*self,control)}\n                fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n                    DslValue::Number(Number::UInt(*self as u64))\n NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(control)?;key.parse().map_err(|_|ValueError::new(\"invalid numeric object key\"))}\n\n                fn from_value_controlled(value:&DslValue,control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{\n                    controlled::scalar(control)?;match value{DslValue::Number(number)=>number.as_u64().and_then(|n| <$ty>::try_from(n).ok()).ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(\"expected exact unsigned integer\")),_=>Err(ValueError::new(\"expected number\"))}\n                }\n                fn default_value_controlled(control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(control)?;Ok(0 as $ty)}\n\n                fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n                    match value {\n                        DslValue::Number(number) => number.as_u64().and_then(|n| <$ty>::try_from(n).ok())\n                            .ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(format!(\"expected an exact {} integer, found {number:?}\", stringify!($ty)))),\n                        other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a number, found {other:?}\"))),\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        )+\n    };\n}\nimpl_uint_codec!(u8, u16, u32, u64, usize);\n\n/// 🔢️ Signed integer scalars — round-trip through [`Number::Int`], same fidelity contract as the\n/// unsigned family above.\nmacro_rules! impl_int_codec {\n    ($($ty:ty),+ $(,)?) => {\n NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{encoding::scalar(control)?;Ok(DslValue::Number(Number::Int(*self as i64)))}\n                fn to_object_key_controlled(&self,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<String,ValueError>{encoding::key(*self,control)}\n                fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n                    DslValue::Number(Number::Int(*self as i64))\n                }\n            }\n            impl FromValue for $ty {\n                fn from_object_key_controlled(key:&str,control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(control)?;key.parse().map_err(|_|ValueError::new(\"invalid numeric object key\"))}\n\n                fn from_value_controlled(value:&DslValue,control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{\n                    controlled::scalar(control)?;match value{DslValue::Number(number)=>number.as_i64().and_then(|n| <$ty>::try_from(n).ok()).ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(\"expected exact signed integer\")),_=>Err(ValueError::new(\"expected number\"))}\n                }\n                fn default_value_controlled(control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(control)?;Ok(0 as $ty)}\n\n                fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n                    match value {\n                        DslValue::Number(number) => number.as_i64().and_then(|n| <$ty>::try_from(n).ok())\n                            .ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(format!(\"expected an exact {} integer, found {number:?}\", stringify!($ty)))),\n                        other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a number, found {other:?}\"))),\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        )+\n    };\n}\nimpl_int_codec!(i8, i16, i32, i64, isize);\n\n/// 🔢️ Fractional scalars — always encode/decode through [`Number::Float`]; a whole float keeps its\n/// explicit `.0` on the wire so it never collapses onto its integer twin.\nmacro_rules! impl_float_codec {\n    ($($ty:ty),+ $(,)?) => {\n        $(\n            impl ToValue for $ty {\n                fn to_value_controlled(&self,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{encoding::scalar(control)?;Ok(DslValue::Number(Number::Float(*self as f64)))}\n                fn to_object_key_controlled(&self,control:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<String,ValueError>{encoding::key(*self,control)}\n                fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n                    DslValue::Number(Number::Float(*self as f64))\n                }\n            }\n            impl FromValue for $ty {\n                fn from_object_key_controlled(key:&str,control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(control)?;key.parse().map_err(|_|ValueError::new(\"invalid numeric object key\"))}\n\n                fn value{DslValue::Number(number)=>Ok(number.as_f64() as $ty),_=>Err(ValueError::new(\"expected number\"))}\n                }\n                fn default_value_controlled(control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(control)?;Ok(0 as $ty)}\n\n                fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n                    match value {\n                        DslValue::Number(n) => Ok(n.as_f64() as $ty),\n                        other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a number, found {other:?}\"))),\n                    }\n                }\n            }\n        )+\n    };\n}\nimpl_float_codec!(f64);\n\nfn float32_from_number(number:Number)->f32{\n    let value=number.as_f64();let bits=value.to_bits();let payload=bits&0x000f_ffff_ffff_ffff;\n    if bits&0x7ff0_0000_0000_0000==0x7ff0_0000_0000_0000&&payload!=0{f32::from_bits(((bits>>32) as u32&0x8000_0000)|0x7f80_0000|((payload>>29) as u32).max(1))}else{value as f32}\n}\n\nimpl ToValue for f32 {\nfn to_value_controlled(&self,c:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{encoding::float32(*self,c)}\nfn to_object_key_controlled(&self,c:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<String,ValueError>{encoding::key(*self,c)}\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        let bits=self.to_bits();let payload=bits&0x007f_ffff;\n        if bits&0x7f80_0000==0x7f80_0000&&payload!=0{return DslValue::Number(Number::Float(f64::from_bits((u64::from(bits&0x8000_0000)<<32)|0x7ff0_0000_0000_0000|(u64::from(payload)<<29))))}\n        let shortest = format!(\"{self:e}\");\n        let precision = shortest.split('e').next().unwrap().bytes().filter(u8::is_ascii_digit).count().saturating_sub(1);\n        DslValue::Number(Number::Float(format!(\"{self:.precision$e}\").parse().expect(\"f32 decimal text is a valid f64\")))\n    }\n}\n\nimpl FromValue for f32 {\nfn from_value_controlled(value:&DslValue,c:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(c)?;match value{DslValue::Number(n)=>Ok(float32_from_number(*n)),_=>Err(ValueError::new(\"expected number\"))}}\nfn default_value_controlled(c:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(c)?;Ok(0.0)}\n\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        match value {\n            DslValue::Number(number) => Ok(float32_from_number(number)),\n            other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a number, found {other:?}\"))),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl ToValue for bool {\nfn to_value_controlled(&self,c:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{encoding::scalar(c)?;Ok(DslValue::Bool(*self))}\nfn to_object_key_controlled(&self,c:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<String,ValueError>{encoding::key(*self,c)}\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        DslValue::Bool(*self)\n    }\n}\nimpl FromValue for bool {\nfn from_object_key_controlled(key:&str,control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(control)?;key.parse().map_err(|_|ValueError::new(\"invalid boolean object key\"))}\n\nfn from_value_controlled(v:&DslValue,c:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(c)?;match v{DslValue::Bool(v)=>Ok(*v),_=>Err(ValueError::new(\"expected bool\"))}}\nfn default_value_controlled(c:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(c)?;Ok(false)}\n\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        match value {\n            DslValue::Bool(b) => Ok(b),\n            other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a bool, found {other:?}\"))),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl ToValue for String {\nfn to_value_controlled(&self,c:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{c.copy_text(self).map(DslValue::String).map_err(ValueError::new)}\nfn to_object_key_controlled(&self,c:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<String,ValueError>{c.copy_text(self).map_err(ValueError::new)}\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        DslValue::String(self.clone())\n    }\n}\nimpl FromValue v{DslValue::String(v)=>c.copy_text(v).map_err(ValueError::new),_=>Err(ValueError::new(\"expected string\"))}}\nfn default_value_controlled(c:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Self,ValueError>{controlled::scalar(c)?;Ok(String::new())}\n\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        match value {\n            DslValue::String(s) => Ok(s),\n            other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a string, found {other:?}\"))),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🗂️ A path renders as its UTF-8 string form (lossy on the encode side — this is a local-only\n/// config value, never a content-addressed hash input, so exact non-Unicode byte round-tripping\n/// is not required the way `serde`'s own `Path`/`PathBuf` impl demands it).\nimpl ToValue for std::path::PathBuf {\nfn to_value_controlled(&self,c:&mut NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{encoding::path(self,c)}\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue::String(s) => Ok(std::path::PathBuf::from(s)),\n            other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a string, found {other:?}\"))),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🌉️ No `FromValue` NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{c.scoped_depth(64,|c|match self{Some(value)=>value.to_value_controlled(c),None=>().to_value_controlled(c)})}\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue integer_from_value_matches_serde_without_coercion() {\n    let fixture: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(include_str!(\"../../🧫️fixtures/🔣️.json\")).expect(\"neutral exact integer corpus\");\n    macro_rules! check {\n            ($($ty:ty),+ $(,)?) => { $(\n                for row in fixture[\"raw\"].as_array().unwrap() {\n                    let raw = row.as_str().unwrap();\n                    let value: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(raw).expect(\"valid JSON scalar\");\n                    let expected = raw.parse::<i128>().is_ok_and(|number| number >= <$ty>::MIN as i128 && assert_eq!(42_i64.to_value(), DslValue::int(42));\n    assert_eq!(i64::from_value(DslValue::int(42)), Ok(42_i64));\n    assert_eq!(true.to_value(), DslValue::Bool(true));\n    assert_eq!(\"hi\".to_string().to_value(), DslValue::String(\"hi\".to_string()));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn option_collapses_nested_none_like_naive_serde() {\n    let outer_none: Option<Option<String>> = None;\n    let inner_none: Option<Option<String>> = Some(None);\n    assert_eq!(outer_none.to_value(), DslValue::Null);\n    assert_eq!(inner_none.to_value(), DslValue::Null);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn vec_round_trips_and_reports_index_on_error() {\n    let values = vec![1_i64, 2, 3];\n    let encoded = values.to_value();\n    assert_eq!(Vec::<i64>::from_value(encoded), Ok(values));\n    let bad = DslValue::Array(vec![DslValue::int(1), DslValue::Bool(true)]);\n    assert_eq!(Vec::<i64>::from_value(bad), Err(ValueError::new(\"1.expected a number, found Bool(true)\")));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn btreemap_round_trips_in_key_order() {\n    let mut map = std::collections::BTreeMap::new();\n    map.insert(\"b\".to_string(), 2_i64);\n    map.insert(\"a\".to_string(), 1_i64);\n    let encoded = map.to_value();\n    assert_eq!(encoded, DslValue::object([(\"a\".to_string(), DslValue::int(1)), (\"b\".to_string(), DslValue::int(2))]));\n    assert_eq!(std::collections::BTreeMap::<String, i64>::from_value(encoded), Ok(map));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn tuple_round_trips_as_two_element_array_like_serde_json() {\n    let pair = (\"a\".to_string(), vec![\"b\".to_string(), \"c\".to_string()]);\n    let encoded = pair.to_value();\n    assert_eq!(encoded, DslValue::Array(vec![DslValue::String(\"a\".to_string()), DslValue::Array(vec![DslValue::String(\"b\".to_string()), i64)>::from_value(bad), Err(ValueError::new(\"expected a 2-element array, found Array([Number(Int(1))])\")));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn fixed_size_array_round_trips_and_rejects_wrong_length() {\n    let values: [f64; 3] = [1.0, 2.0, 3.0];\n    let encoded = values.to_value();\n    assert_eq!(encoded, DslValue::Array(vec![DslValue::float(1.0), DslValue::float(2.0), DslValue::float(3.0)]));\n    assert_eq!(<[f64; 3]>::from_value(encoded), Ok(values));\n\n    let too_short = DslValue::Array(vec![DslValue::float(1.0), DslValue::float(2.0)]);\n    assert_eq!(<[f64; 3]>::from_value(too_short), phantom_data_encodes_as_null_and_decodes_from_anything() {\n    struct Marker;\n    let phantom: std::marker::PhantomData<Marker> = std::marker::PhantomData;\n    assert_eq!(phantom.to_value(), f32_widens_through_its_own_shortest_lexeme_not_its_bits() {\n    let fixture: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(include_str!(\"../../🧫️fixtures/🔢️f32-decimals.json\")).expect(\"float decimal fixture\");\n    for case in fixture[\"cases\"].as_array().unwrap() {\n        let value = f32::from_bits(u32::from_str_radix(case[\"bits\"].as_str().unwrap(), 16).unwrap());\n        let decimal = case[\"decimal\"].as_str().unwrap();\n        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_string(&value).unwrap(), decimal);\n        assert_eq!(f64::from_value(value.to_value()).unwrap().to_bits(), decimal.parse::<f64>().unwrap().to_bits());\n    }\n    for value in [0.42_f32, 1.1, 3.14159, 1e-7, 16777217.0, -0.02, 0.85, 0.0625, f32::MIN_POSITIVE, f32::MAX, f32::from_bits(1)] {\n        let DslValue::Number(Number::Float(widened)) = value.to_value() else {\n            panic!(\"f32 must encode as Number::Float, found {:?}\", value.to_value());\n        };\n        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_string(&widened).expect(\"finite f64\"), serde_json::to_string(&value).expect(\"finite f32\"), \"widened lexeme must equal serde_json's own f32 lexeme for {value:e}\");\n        assert_eq!(f32::from_value(value.to_value()), Ok(value), \"narrowing back must be exact for {value:e}\");\n    }\n    assert_eq!((0.42_f32).to_value(), DslValue::float(0.42));\n}\n\n/// 🔬️ Deterministic sweep over arbitrary `f32` bit patterns — every finite `f32` must survive\n/// `to_value`/`from_value` bit-exactly (this is what keeps the binary record carriers, which\n/// store `Number::Float`'s `f64` verbatim, lossless for `f32` fields) AND must widen to a\n/// `f64` equal to serde's parsed decimal value. Serde uses different fixed/scientific\n/// notation thresholds for f32 and f64, so spelling equality is not a numeric invariant.\n#[test]\nfn every_finite_f32_round_trips_bit_exactly_and_preserves_serde_decimal_value() {\n    let mut state: u64 = 0x9E37_79B9_7F4A_7C15;\n    let mut checked = 0usize;\n    for _ in 0..200_000u32 {\n        state = state.wrapping_mul(6364136223846793005).wrapping_add(1442695040888963407);\n        let value = f32::from_bits((state >> 32) as u32);\n        if !value.is_finite() {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let encoded = value.to_value();\n        let DslValue::Number(Number::Float(widened)) = encoded else { panic!(\"f32 must encode as Number::Float\") };\n        let reference: f64 = serde_json::to_string(&value).expect(\"finite f32\").parse().expect(\"decimal f64\");\n        assert_eq!(widened.to_bits(), reference.to_bits(), \"decimal value mismatch for f32 bits {:#010x}\", value.to_bits());\n        assert_eq!(f32::from_value(encoded).expect(\"float\").to_bits(), value.to_bits(), \"bit mismatch for f32 bits {:#010x}\", value.to_bits());\n        checked += 1;\n    }\n    assert!(checked > 150_000, \"sweep must reach a real sample count, got {checked}\");\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn whole_float_and_same_valued_integer_are_distinct_dsl_values() {\n    let as_float = DslValue::float(3600.0);\n    let as_uint = DslValue::uint(3600);\n    assert_ne!(as_float, as_uint);\n    assert!(matches!(as_float, DslValue::Number(Number::Float(_))));\n    assert!(matches!(as_uint, DslValue::Number(Number::UInt(_))));\n}\n",

fixture\");\n    for case in fixture[\"cases\"].as_array().unwrap() {\n        let value = f32::from_bits(u32::from_str_radix(case[\"bits\"].as_str().unwrap(), 16).unwrap());\n        let decimal = std::mem::ManuallyDrop;\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n\n#[path = \"🧺️set/🦀️.rs\"]\npub mod set;\npub use set::OrderedSet;\n\n//#region 🌳️PersistentNodes\ntype Root<V> = Option<Arc<Node<V>>>;\n/// 📏️ Fixed metadata-visit bound for one rank-iterator item; no payload bytes are read by iteration.\npub const MAX_AVL_HEIGHT: usize = 2 * usize::BITS as usize;\nstruct Entry<V> { key: Arc<String>, value: Arc<V> }\nstruct Node<V> { entry: Arc<Entry<V>>, left: Root<V>, right: Root<V>, height: usize, len: usize }\n\nimpl<V> Clone for Entry<V> {\n    fn clone(&self) -> Self { Self { key: Arc::clone(&self.key), value: Arc::clone(&self.value) } }\n}\nimpl<V> Clone for Node<V> {\n    fn clone(&self) -> Self { Self { entry: Arc::clone(&self.entry), left: self.left.clone(), right: self.right.clone(), height: self.height, len: self.len } }\n}\n\nfn height<V>(root: &Root<V>) -> usize { root.as_ref().map_or(0, |value| value.height) }\nfn len<V>(root: &Root<V>) -> usize { root.as_ref().map_or(0, |value| value.len) }\nfn node<V>(entry: Arc<Entry<V>>, left: Root<V>, right: Root<V>) -> Arc<Node<V>> {\n    let height = 1 + height(&left).max(height(&right));\n    assert!(height <= MAX_AVL_HEIGHT, \"ordered-map fixed metadata frontier exceeded\");\n    Arc::new(Node { height, len: 1 + len(&left) + len(&right), entry, left, right })\n}\n\nfn balanced<V>(entry: Arc<Entry<V>>, left: Root<V>, right: Root<V>) -> Arc<Node<V>> {\n    if height(&left) > height(&right) + 1 {\n        let branch = left.as_ref().unwrap();\n        if height(&branch.left) >= height(&branch.right) {\n            let right = node(entry, branch.right.clone(), right);\n            return node(Arc::clone(&branch.entry), branch.left.clone(), Some(right));\n        }\n        let pivot = branch.right.as_ref().unwrap();\n        let left = node(Arc::clone(&branch.entry), branch.left.clone(), pivot.left.clone());\n        let right = node(entry, pivot.right.clone(), right);\n        return node(Arc::clone(&pivot.entry), Some(left), Some(right));\n    }\n    if height(&right) > height(&left) + 1 {\n        let branch = right.as_ref().unwrap();\n        if height(&branch.right) >= height(&branch.left) {\n            let left = node(entry, left, branch.left.clone());\n            return node(Arc::clone(&branch.entry), Some(left), branch.right.clone());\n        }\n        let pivot = branch.left.as_ref().unwrap();\n        let left = node(entry, left, pivot.left.clone());\n        let right = node(Arc::clone(&branch.entry), pivot.right.clone(), branch.right.clone());\n        return node(Arc::clone(&pivot.entry), Some(left), Some(right));\n    }\n    node(entry, left, right)\n}\n\nfn at<V>(mut root: &Root<V>, mut index: usize) -> Option<&Entry<V>> {\n    loop {\n        let current = root.as_ref()?;\n        match index.cmp(&len(&current.left)) {\n            Ordering::Less => root = &current.left,\n            Ordering::Equal => return Some(&current.entry),\n            Ordering::Greater => { index -= len(&current.left) + 1; root = &current.right; }\n        }\n    }\n}\n//#endregion 🌳️PersistentNodes\n\n//#region 🗂️Map\n/// 🗂️ Ordered immutable root; clones share payloads and every nonempty owner must be explicitly retired.\n/// 🔒️ Dropping live ownership panics without destroying payloads; unwinding preserves it without a second panic.\n#[must_use = \"ordered roots must be transferred or explicitly retired\"]\npub struct OrderedMap<V> { root: ManuallyDrop<Root<V>> }\n\nimpl<V> Default for OrderedMap<V> { fn default() -> Self { Self { root: ManuallyDrop::new(None) } } }\nimpl<V> Clone for OrderedMap<V> { fn clone(&self) -> Self { Self { root: self.root.clone() } } }\nimpl<V> Drop for OrderedMap<V> {\n    fn drop(&mut self) { if !std::thread::panicking() { assert!(self.root.is_none(), \"ordered-map root must be explicitly retired before drop\"); } }\n}\n\nimpl<V> OrderedMap<V> {\n    pub fn new() -> Self { Self::default() }\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize { len(&self.root) }\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool { self.root.is_none() }\n    pub fn iter(&self) -> Iter<'_, V> { Iter { root: &self.root, front: 0, back: self.len() } }\n    pub fn keys(&self) -> impl DoubleEndedIterator<Item = &String> + ExactSizeIterator { self.iter().map(|(key, _)| key) }\n    pub fn values(&self) -> impl DoubleEndedIterator<Item = &V> + ExactSizeIterator { self.iter().map(|(_, value)| value) }\n    pub fn first_key_value(&self) -> Option<(&String, &V)> { self.iter().next() }\n    /// 📍️ Borrows one ranked entry with at most MAX_AVL_HEIGHT metadata visits; charge one retained item.\n    pub fn entry_at_rank(&self, index: usize) -> Option<(&String, &V)> { at(&self.root, index).map(|entry| (entry.key.as_ref(), root: &Root<V> = &self.root;\n        loop {\n            let current = root.as_ref()?;\n            match key.cmp(current.entry.key.as_str()) {\n                Ordering::Less => root = &current.left, Ordering::Greater => root = &current.right,\n                Ordering::Equal => return Some(&current.entry.value),\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    /// 🧊️ Cold synchronous membership; no interactive accounting is provided.\n    pub fn contains_key(&self, key: &str) -> bool { self.get(key).is_some() }\n\n    /// ✏️ Begins an upsert by moving inline V; retained callers must admit its inline size or use begin_set_shared.\n    pub fn begin_set(&self, key: String, value: V) -> UpdateCursor<V> { self.begin_set_shared(Arc::new(key), Arc::new(value)) }\n    /// 📥️ Begins a retained upsert by moving exactly two shared pointers; no key or value bytes are copied.\n    pub fn begin_set_shared(&self, key: Arc<String>, value: Arc<V>) -> UpdateCursor<V> { UpdateCursor::new(self.clone(), key, Some(value)) }\n    /// 🗑️ Begins a retained removal; missing keys leave an identical shared root.\n    pub fn begin_remove(&self, key: String) -> UpdateCursor<V> { self.begin_remove_shared(Arc::new(key)) }\n    /// 🗑️ Moves an exact shared key into retained removal without copying its bytes.\n    pub fn begin_remove_shared(&self, key: Arc<String>) -> UpdateCursor<V> { UpdateCursor::new(self.clone(), key, None) }\n    /// 🔎️ Retains an immutable root and compares a lookup key under the caller's byte grants.\n    pub fn begin_lookup(&self, key: String) -> LookupCursor<V> { self.begin_lookup_shared(Arc::new(key)) }\n    /// 🔎️ Moves an exact shared key into retained lookup without copying its bytes.\n    pub fn begin_lookup_shared(&self, key: Arc<String>) -> LookupCursor<V> { LookupCursor::new(self.clone(), key) }\n\n    /// ⚡️ Completes a synchronous convenience upsert; retained jobs must use begin_set and advance.\n    pub fn insert(&mut self, key: String, value: V) -> Option<Arc<V>> {\n        let mut cursor = self.begin_set(key, value);\n        while !cursor.is_complete() { cursor.advance(Grant { maximum_items: 1, maximum_bytes: 4096 }); }\n        let removed = cursor.take_removed(); let displaced = std::mem::replace(self, cursor.take_result().unwrap()); retire_cold(displaced.retire()); close_cold(&mut cursor); removed\n    }\n    /// ⚡️ Completes a synchronous convenience removal; retained jobs must use begin_remove and advance.\n    pub fn remove(&mut self, key: &str) -> Option<Arc<V>> {\n        let mut cursor =  pub fn retire(mut self) -> Retirement<V> { Retirement::new(self.root.take()) }\n    /// 📤️ Atomically releases a shared root or transfers its exact final ownership without traversing payloads.\n    pub fn release_shared(mut self) -> Result<(), Retirement<V>> {\n        let Some(root) = self.root.take() else { return Ok(()); };\n        let Some(node) = Arc::into_inner(root) else { return Ok(()); };\n        let mut retirement = Retirement::default();\n        if let Some(left) = node.left { retirement.push(Owner::Node(left)); }\n        if let Some(right) = node.right { nodes without reading payload bytes.\n/// 🎟️ Retained consumers must account each next/next_back as one fixed metadata item.\npub struct Iter<'a, V> { root: &'a Root<V>, front: usize, back: usize metadata-visit bound for one rank-iterator item; no payload bytes are read by iteration.\npub const MAX_AVL_HEIGHT: usize = 2 * usize::BITS as usize;\nstruct Entry<V> { key: Arc<String>, value: Arc<V> }\nstruct Node<V> { entry: Arc<Entry<V>>, left: Root<V>, right: Root<V>, height: usize, len: usize }\n\nimpl<V> Clone for Entry<V> {\n    fn clone(&self) -> Self { Self { key: Arc::clone(&self.key), value: Arc::clone(&self.value) } }\n}\nimpl<V> Clone for Node<V> {\n    fn clone(&self) -> Self { Self { entry: Arc::clone(&self.entry), left: self.left.clone(), right: self.right.clone(), height: self.height, len: self.len } }\n}\n\nfn height<V>(root: &Root<V>) -> usize { root.as_ref().map_or(0, |value| value.height) }\nfn len<V>(root: &Root<V>) -> usize { root.as_ref().map_or(0, |value| value.len) }\nfn node<V>(entry: Arc<Entry<V>>, left: Root<V>, right: Root<V>) -> Arc<Node<V>> {\n    let height = 1 + height(&left).max(height(&right));\n    assert!(height <= MAX_AVL_HEIGHT, \"ordered-map fixed metadata frontier exceeded\");\n    Arc::new(Node { height, len: 1 + len(&left) + len(&right), entry, left, right })\n}\n\nfn balanced<V>(entry: Arc<Entry<V>>, left: Root<V>, right: Root<V>) -> Arc<Node<V>> {\n    if height(&left) > height(&right) + 1 {\n        let branch = left.as_ref().unwrap();\n        if height(&branch.left) >= height(&branch.right) {\n            let right = node(entry, branch.right.clone(), right);\n            return node(Arc::clone(&branch.entry), branch.left.clone(), Some(right));\n        }\n        let pivot = branch.right.as_ref().unwrap();\n        let left = node(Arc::clone(&branch.entry), branch.left.clone(), pivot.left.clone());\n        let right = node(entry, pivot.right.clone(), right);\n        return node(Arc::clone(&pivot.entry), Some(left), Some(right));\n    }\n    if height(&right) > height(&left) + 1 {\n        let branch = right.as_ref().unwrap();\n        if height(&branch.right) >= height(&branch.left) {\n            let left = node(entry, left, branch.left.clone());\n            return node(Arc::clone(&branch.entry), Some(left), branch.right.clone());\n        }\n        let pivot = branch.left.as_ref().unwrap();\n        let left = node(entry, left, pivot.left.clone());\n        let right = node(Arc::clone(&branch.entry), pivot.right.clone(), branch.right.clone());\n        return node(Arc::clone(&pivot.entry), Some(left), Some(right));\n    }\n    node(entry, left, right)\n}\n\nfn at<V>(mut root: &Root<V>, mut index: usize) -> Option<&Entry<V>> {\n    loop {\n        let current = root.as_ref()?;\n        match index.cmp(&len(&current.left)) {\n            Ordering::Less => root = &current.left,\n            Ordering::Equal => return Some(&current.entry),\n            Ordering::Greater => { index -= len(&current.left) + 1; root = &current.right; }\n        }\n    }\n}\n//#endregion 🌳️PersistentNodes\n\n//#region 🗂️Map\n/// 🗂️ Ordered immutable root; clones share payloads and every nonempty owner must be explicitly retired.\n/// 🔒️ Dropping live ownership panics without destroying payloads; unwinding preserves it without a second panic.\n#[must_use = \"ordered roots must be transferred or explicitly retired\"]\npub struct OrderedMap<V> { root: ManuallyDrop<Root<V>> }\n\nimpl<V> Default for OrderedMap<V> { fn default() -> Self { Self { root: ManuallyDrop::new(None) } } }\nimpl<V> Clone for OrderedMap<V> { fn clone(&self) -> Self { Self { root: self.root.clone() } } }\nimpl<V> Drop for OrderedMap<V> {\n    fn drop(&mut self) { if !std::thread::panicking() { assert!(self.root.is_none(), \"ordered-map root must be explicitly retired before drop\"); } }\n}\n\nimpl<V> OrderedMap<V> {\n    pub fn new() -> Self { Self::default() }\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize { len(&self.root) }\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool { self.root.is_none() }\n    pub fn iter(&self) -> Iter<'_, V> { Iter { root: &self.root, front: 0, back: self.len() } }\n    pub fn keys(&self) -> impl DoubleEndedIterator<Item = &String> + ExactSizeIterator { self.iter().map(|(key, _)| key) }\n    pub fn values(&self) -> impl DoubleEndedIterator<Item = &V> + ExactSizeIterator { self.iter().map(|(_, value)| value) }\n    pub fn first_key_value(&self) -> Option<(&String, &V)> { self.iter().next() }\n    /// 📍️ Borrows one ranked entry with at most MAX_AVL_HEIGHT metadata visits; charge one retained item.\n    pub fn entry_at_rank(&self, index: usize) -> Option<(&String, &V)> { at(&self.root, index).map(|entry| (entry.key.as_ref(), entry.value.as_ref())) }\n    /// 🧊️ Cold synchronous lookup; retained callers must use begin_lookup to account comparison bytes.\n    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&V> {\n        let mut root: &Root<V> = &self.root;\n        loop {\n            let current = root.as_ref()?;\n            match key.cmp(current.entry.key.as_str()) {\n                Ordering::Less => root = &current.left, Ordering::Greater => root = &current.right,\n                Ordering::Equal => return Some(&current.entry.value),\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    /// 🧊️ Cold synchronous membership; no interactive accounting is provided.\n    pub fn contains_key(&self, key: &str) -> bool { self.get(key).is_some() }\n\n    /// ✏️ Begins an upsert by moving inline V; retained callers must admit its inline size or use begin_set_shared.\n    pub fn begin_set(&self, key: String, value: V) -> UpdateCursor<V> { self.begin_set_shared(Arc::new(key), Arc::new(value)) }\n    /// 📥️ Begins UpdateCursor::new(self.clone(), key, Some(value)) }\n    /// 🗑️ Begins a retained removal; missing keys leave an identical shared root.\n    pub fn begin_remove(&self, key: String) -> UpdateCursor<V> { self.begin_remove_shared(Arc::new(key)) }\n    /// 🗑️ Moves an exact shared key into retained removal without copying its bytes.\n    pub fn begin_remove_shared(&self, key: Arc<String>) -> UpdateCursor<V> { UpdateCursor::new(self.clone(), key, None) }\n    /// 🔎️ Retains an immutable root and compares a lookup key under the caller's byte grants.\n    pub fn begin_lookup(&self, key:
