self, key: String, value: V) -> Option<Arc<V>> {\n        let mut cursor = self.begin_set(key, value);\n        while !cursor.is_complete() { cursor.advance(Grant { maximum_items: 1, maximum_bytes: 4096 }); }\n        let removed = cursor.take_removed(); let displaced = std::mem::replace(self, cursor.take_result().unwrap()); retire_cold(displaced.retire()); close_cold(&mut cursor); removed\n    }\n    /// ⚡️ Completes a synchronous convenience removal; retained jobs must use begin_remove and advance.\n    pub fn remove(&mut self, key: &str) -> Option<Arc<V>> {\n        let mut cursor = self.begin_remove(key.to_owned());\n        while !cursor.is_complete() { cursor.advance(Grant { maximum_items: 1, maximum_bytes: 4096 }); }\n        let removed = cursor.take_removed(); let displaced = std::mem::replace(self, cursor.take_result().unwrap()); retire_cold(displaced.retire()); close_cold(&mut cursor); removed\n    }\n    /// 🧹️ Moves this root into explicit final-owner retirement.\n    pub fn retire(mut self) -> Retirement<V> { Retirement::new(self.root.take()) }\n    /// 📤️ Atomically releases a shared root or transfers its exact final ownership without traversing payloads.\n    pub fn release_shared(mut self) -> Result<(), Retirement<V>> {\n        let Some(root) = self.root.take() else { return Ok(()); };\n        let Some(node) = Arc::into_inner(root) else { return Ok(()); };\n        let mut retirement = Retirement::default();\n        if let Some(left) = node.left { retirement.push(Owner::Node(left)); }\n        if let Some(right) = node.right { nodes without reading payload bytes.\n/// 🎟️ Retained consumers must account each next/next_back as one fixed metadata item.\npub struct Iter<'a, V> { root: &'a Root<V>, front: usize, back: usize }\nimpl<'a, V> Iterator for Iter<'a, V> {\n    type Item = (&'a String, &'a V);\n    fn next(&mut self) -> Option<Self::Item> {\n        if self.front == self.back { return None; }\n        let entry structural phase or a byte-bounded comparison fragment.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Grant { pub maximum_items: usize, pub maximum_bytes: usize }\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Step { Blocked, Progress { completed_items: usize, completed_bytes: usize }, Complete }\n\nfn compare_bytes(key: &[u8], other: &[u8], offset: &mut usize, left_byte: &mut Option<u8>, ordering: &mut Option<Ordering>, maximum_bytes: usize) -> usize {\n    let mut bytes = 0;\n    while ordering.is_none() && bytes < maximum_bytes {\n        if *offset == key.len().min(other.len()) { *ordering = Some(key.len().cmp(&other.len())); break; }\n        if let Some(left) = left_byte.take() {\n            let right = other[*offset]; bytes += 1; *offset += 1;\n            if left != right { *ordering = Some(left.cmp(&right)); }\n        } else { *left_byte = Some(key[*offset]); bytes += 1; }\n    }\n    bytes\n}\n\nenum Phase { Search, Successor, bound.\nstruct UpdateState<V> {\n    base: OrderedMap<V>, key: Option<Arc<String>>, value: Option<Arc<V>>, current: Root<V>, path: LinkedList<Parent<V>>,\n    successor_path: LinkedList<Arc<Node<V>>>, maximum_bytes: usize) -> usize {\n        compare_bytes(self.key.as_ref().unwrap().as_bytes(), self.current.as_ref().unwrap().entry.key.as_bytes(), &mut self.offset, &mut self.left_byte, &mut self.ordering, maximum_bytes)\n    }\n\n    pub fn advance(&mut self, grant: Grant) -> Step {\n        if self.closing || grant.maximum_items == 0 || grant.maximum_bytes == 0 { return Step::Blocked; }\n        let mut bytes = 0;\n        match self.phase {\n            Phase::Search => {\n                if self.current.is_none() {\n                    self.replacement = self.value.as_ref().map(|value| node(Arc::new(Entry { key: Arc::clone(self.key.as_ref().unwrap()), value: Arc::clone(value) }), None, None));\n                    self.phase = Phase::Rebuild;\n                } else if self.ordering.is_none() { bytes = self.compare(grant.maximum_bytes); }\n                else {\n                    let current = self.current.take().unwrap();\n                    match self.ordering.take().unwrap() {\n                        ordering @ (Ordering::Less | Ordering::Greater) => {\n                            let direction = ordering == Ordering::Less;\n                            self.current = if direction { current.left.clone() } else { current.right.clone() };\n                            self.path.push_front(Parent { node: current, left: direction });\n                        }\n                        Ordering::Equal => {\n                            self.removed = Some(Arc::clone(&current.entry.value));\n                            if let Some(value) = &self.value {\n                                self.replacement = Some(node(Arc::new(Entry { key: Arc::clone(self.key.as_ref().unwrap()), value: Arc::clone(value) }), current.left.clone(), Some(balanced(Arc::clone(&parent.entry), self.replacement.take(), parent.right.clone())); }\n                else {\n                    let removed = self.removed_node.take().unwrap();\n                    self.replacement = Some(balanced(self.successor_entry.take().unwrap(), removed.left.clone(), self.replacement.take())); self.phase = Phase::Rebuild;\n                }\n            }\n            Phase::Rebuild => {\n                if let Some(parent) = self.path.pop_front() {\n                    self.replacement = Some(if parent.left { balanced(Arc::clone(&parent.node.entry), self.replacement.take(), parent.node.right.clone()) }\n                        else { balanced(Arc::clone(&parent.node.entry), parent.node.left.clone(), self.replacement.take()) });\n                }   }\n        Step::Progress { completed_items: 1, completed_bytes: bytes }\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_complete(&self) -> bool { matches!(self.phase, Phase::Complete) }\n    pub fn take_result(&mut self) -> Option<OrderedMap<V>> { self.result.take() }\n    pub fn take_removed(&mut self) -> Option<Arc<V>> { self.removed.take() }\n    pub fn begin_close(&mut self) { self.closing = true; }\n\n    pub fn close_step(&mut self, grant: Grant) -> RetirementStep<V> {\n        if !self.closing || grant.maximum_items == 0 || grant.maximum_bytes == 0 { return RetirementStep::Blocked; }\n        if else { return RetirementStep::Complete; }\n        RetirementStep::Progress { released_items: 1, released_bytes: 0 }\n    }\n\n    pub fn terminal_is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.closing && self.base.is_empty() && self.key.is_none() && self.value.is_none() && self.current.is_none() && self.path.is_empty()\n            && self.successor_path.is_empty() && self.removed_node.is_none() && self.successor_entry.is_none() && self.replacement.is_none()\n            && self.removed.is_none() && self.result.is_none() && self.retirement.is_empty()\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🔒️ Terminal guard prevents key, value)) } }\n    pub fn advance(&mut self, grant: Grant) -> Step { self.state.advance(grant) }\n    /// 🛬️ Admits an insert's concrete node and path allocations before one byte-bounded update };\n        control.checkpoint()?;\n        control.charge(bytes)?;\n        Ok(self.advance(grant))\n    }\n    pub fn is_complete(&self) -> bool { self.state.is_complete() }\n    pub fn       "source": "//! 🌱️ `DslValue` — the schema-erased dynamic value both sides of a replication link speak.\n//!\n//! Lives beside the wire contract rather than inside the os DSL because it is what a schema-less\n//! payload decodes to: the authority validates it, the optimistic replica applies it, and the\n//! pathmap bodies `db` stores are trees of it. The DSL's own record/field/wire types build on it\n//! and stay product-side.\n// 🚫️async: E1 pure accessor consumed by external-trait impls (serde/Display) — see R9\n\n//#region 🗂️OrderedOwnership\n#[path = \"🗂️ordered/🦀️.rs\"]\npub mod ordered;\n#[path = \"📋️list/🦀️.rs\"]\npub mod list;\n#[path = \"📦️paged/🦀️.rs\"]\npub mod paged;\n//#endregion 🗂️OrderedOwnership\n\n#[path = \"🧬️bytes/🦀️.rs\"]\npub mod bytes;\n\n#[path = \"🧬️clone/🦀️.rs\"]\npub mod bounded_clone;\n\n#[path = \"🛬️decode/🦀️.rs\"]\npub mod native_decoding;\npub use native_decoding::NativeDecodeControl;\n\n#[path = \"🛫️encode/🦀️.rs\"]\npub mod native_encoding;\npub use native_encoding::NativeEncodeControl;\n\n//#region 🔁️Codec\n#[path = \"🔁️codec/🦀️.rs\"]\nmod codec;\npub use codec::{edit_through_value, ControlledValueHasher, DecodedValue, FromValue, ToValue, ValueEdit, ValueError, ValueShape};\n//#endregion 🔁️Codec\n\n//#region 🔖️Number\n/// 🔢️ A JSON-equivalent number that keeps the writer's-eye distinction a bare `f64` erases:\n/// an integer literal (`UInt`/`Int`) round-trips without a decimal point, `Float` always keeps one\n/// (or an exponent). Mirrors [`pack::json::Number`]'s shape exactly so the wire bridge between them\n/// (`🎒️pack/🔤️json/🦀️.rs`) is a straight variant-to-variant map, never a widen-then-guess. See\n/// `.🧬semio/🦑️repo/🎫️tickets/🎆️26/🌙️09/☀️01/RUNTIME-DEPENDENCY-ELIMINATION-FOR-S-PLUGINS-AND-ARTIFACTS/\n/// 🔍️research/📓️dslvalue-integer-fidelity.md`.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug)]\npub enum Number {\n    UInt(u64),\n    Int(i64),\n    Float(f64),\n}\n\nimpl Number {\n    /// 🔎️ Widens to `f64` regardless of variant — lossy for `u64`/`i64` magnitudes beyond 2^53.\n    pub fn as_f64(&self) -> f64 {\n        match *self {\n            Number::UInt(v) => v as f64,\n            Number::Int(v) => v as f64,\n            Number::Float(v) => v,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 🔎️ Exact `i64`, only for the `Int` variant and `UInt` values that fit.\n    pub fn as_i64(&self) -> Option<i64> {\n        match *self {\n            Number::Int(v) => Some(v),\n            Number::UInt(v) => i64::try_from(v).ok(),\n            Number::Float(_) => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 🔎️ Exact `u64`, only for the `UInt` variant and non-negative `Int` values.\n    pub fn as_u64(&self) -> Option<u64> {\n        match *self {\n            Number::UInt(v) => Some(v),\n            Number::Int(v) => u64::try_from(v).ok(),\n            Number::Float(_) => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 🔎️ Whether this literal was written without a decimal point or exponent.\n    pub fn is_integer(&self) -> bool {\n        !matches!(self, Number::Float(_))\n    }\n}\n\nimpl PartialEq for Number {\n    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {\n        match (*self, *other) {\n            (Number::UInt(a), Number::UInt(b)) => a == b,\n            (Number::Int(a), Number::Int(b)) => a == b,\n            (Number::Float(a), Number::Float(b)) => a == b,\n            (Number::UInt(a), Number::Int(b)) | (Number::Int(b), Number::UInt(a)) => i64::try_from(a).is_ok_and(|a| a == b),\n            _ => false,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl From<u64> for Number {\n    fn from(v: u64) -> Self {\n        Number::UInt(v)\n    }\n}\nimpl From<i64> for Number {\n    fn from(v: i64) -> Self {\n        Number::Int(v)\n    }\n}\nimpl From<f64> for Number {\n    fn from(v: f64) -> Self {\n        Number::Float(v)\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🔢️ The integer one finite JSON number reads back as — [`json_integer`]'s answer.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum JsonInteger {\n    Unsigned(u64),\n    Signed(i64),\n}\n\n/// 🔢️ The integer an `f64` reads back as from its JSON text: `JSON.stringify(7.0)` is `\"7\"`, so a finite, integral number\n/// within the safe integer range (`Number.isSafeInteger`, |v| ≤ 2^53 − 1) is an integer — unsigned unless negative — and\n/// anything else (a fraction, a non-finite value, an integral value past the safe range) is not. The ONE rule every Rust\n/// boundary that carries a JSON number as `f64` reads it by (`DslValue::json_number`, the UI contract's `UiValue` serializer).\npub fn json_integer(v: f64) -> Option<JsonInteger> {\n    const SAFE_INTEGER_MAX: f64 = 9_007_199_254_740_991.0;\n    if !v.is_finite() || v.fract() != 0.0 || v.abs() > SAFE_INTEGER_MAX {\n        return None;\n    }\n    Some(if v >= 0.0 { JsonInteger::Unsigned(v as u64) } else { JsonInteger::Signed(v as i64) })\n}\n//#endregion 🔖️Number\n\n//#region 🔖️Value\n/// 🌱️ Dynamic JSON-equivalent literal for schema-less fields (`Shape::Value`).\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]\npub enum DslValue {\n    Null,\n    Bool(bool),\n    Number(Number),\n    String(String),\n    Bytes(Vec<u8>),\n    Array(Vec<DslValue>),\n    Object(Vec<(String, DslValue)>),\n}\n\n/// 🪪️ Immutable framework value selected from one retained domain owner.\npub trait DslValueSource {\n    fn value(&self) -> &DslValue;\n}\n\nimpl DslValueSource for std::sync::Arc<DslValue> {\n    fn value(&self) -> &DslValue { self.as_ref() }\n}\n\nimpl DslValue {\n    pub fn null() -> Self {\n        Self::Null\n    }\n\n    /// 🔢️ Whole-number constructor — the fidelity-preserving choice for ids/counts/indices/ms.\n    pub fn uint(v: u64) -> Self {\n        Self::Number(Number::UInt(v))\n    }\n\n    /// 🔢️ Signed whole-number constructor.\n    pub fn int(v: i64) -> Self {\n        Self::Number(Number::Int(v))\n    }\n\n    /// 🔢️ Fractional constructor — the wire always keeps an explicit `.0` for a whole float so it\n    /// never collapses onto its integer twin.\n    pub fn float(v: f64) -> Self {\n        Self::Number(Number::Float(v))\n    }\n\n    /// 🔢️ A JSON number carried as `f64` (the UI contract's `UiValue::Number`), read the way its JSON text reads back\n    /// ([`json_integer`]): an integer stays an integer, a non-finite value is `Null` (JSON text has neither NaN nor Infinity),\n    /// anything else a float — so an integer argument a renderer hands back decodes as the integer React's wire delivers.\n    pub fn json_number(v: f64) -> Self {\n        match json_integer(v) {\n            Some(JsonInteger::Unsigned(value)) => Self::uint(value),\n            Some(JsonInteger::Signed(value)) => Self::int(value),\n            None if v.is_finite() => Self::float(v),\n            None => Self::Null,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_null(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, Self::Null)\n    }\n\n    pub fn as_bool(&self) -> Option<bool> {\n        match self {\n            Self::Bool(b) => Some(*b),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 🔎️ Widens to `f64` regardless of variant — lossy for `u64`/`i64` magnitudes beyond 2^53. Use\n    /// [`DslValue::as_i64`]/[`DslValue::as_u64`] when exactness matters.\n    pub fn as_f64(&self) -> Option<f64> {\n        match self {\n            Self::Number(n) => Some(n.as_f64()),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 🔎️ Exact `i64`, only when the underlying [`Number`] is representable as one.\n    pub fn as_i64(&self) -> Option<i64> {\n        match self {\n            Self::Number(n) => n.as_i64(),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 🔎️ Exact `u64`, only when the underlying [`Number`] is representable as one.\n    pub fn as_u64(&self) -> Option<u64> {\n        match self {\n            Self::Number(n) => n.as_u64(),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> Option<&str> {\n        match self {\n            Self::String(s) => Some(s.as_str()),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 🧬️ Borrows intrinsic octets without projecting one numeric node per byte.\n    pub fn as_bytes(&self)->Option<&[u8]>{match self{Self::Bytes(bytes)=>Some(bytes),_=>None}}\n\n    pub fn as_array(&self) -> Option<&[DslValue]> {\n        match self {\n            Self::Array(items) => Some(items.as_slice()),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn as_object(&self) -> Option<&[(String, DslValue)]> {\n        match self {\n            Self::Object(entries) => Some(entries.as_slice()),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n\n    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&DslValue> {\n        let Self::Object(entries) = self else {\n            return None;\n        };\n        entries.iter().find(|(k, _)| k == key).map(|(_, v)| v)\n    }\n\n    pub fn object(entries: impl IntoIterator<Item = (String, DslValue)>) -> Self {\n        Self::Object(entries.into_iter().collect())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::ops::Index<&str> for DslValue {\n    type Output = DslValue;\n    fn index(&self, key: &str) -> &Self::Output {\n        static NULL: DslValue = DslValue::Null;\n        self.get(key).unwrap_or(&NULL)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::ops::Index<usize> for DslValue {\n    type Output = DslValue;\n    fn index(&self, index: usize) -> &Self::Output {\n        static NULL: DslValue = DslValue::Null;\n        match self {\n            DslValue::Array(items) => items.get(index).unwrap_or(&NULL),\n            _ => &NULL,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl From<&DslValue> for serde_json::Value {\n    fn from(val: &DslValue) -> Self {\n        match val {\n            DslValue::Null => serde_json::Value::Null,\n            DslValue::Bool(b) => serde_json::Value::Bool(*b),\n            DslValue::Number(Number::UInt(v)) => serde_json::Value::Number((*v).into()),\n            DslValue::Number(Number::Int(v)) => serde_json::Value::Number((*v).into()),\n            DslValue::Number(Number::Float(v)) => serde_json::json!(*v),\n            DslValue::String(s) => serde_json::Value::String(s.clone()),\n            DslValue::Bytes(bytes) => serde_json::Value::Array(bytes.iter().map(|byte|serde_json::Value::Number((*byte).into())).collect()),\n            DslValue::Array(arr) => serde_json::Value::Array(arr.iter().map(serde_json::Value::from).collect()),\n            DslValue::Object(obj) => {\n                let map = obj.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), serde_json::Value::from(v))).collect();\n                serde_json::Value::Object(map)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl From<DslValue> for serde_json::Value {\n    fn from(val: DslValue) -> Self {\n        serde_json::Value::from(&val)\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🌉️ The reverse bridge: a plugin decoding `ArtifactEditor::command_from_action`/\n/// `host_configuration_mutation`'s trait-mandated `Option<&serde_json::Value>` args into a\n/// `ToValue`/`FromValue` domain type routes through here — preserves whichever of `serde_json`'s\n/// own `u64`/`i64`/`f64` storage the number parsed into (same convention `pack::json`'s\n/// `to_dsl_value` bridge uses for its sibling `Value` type), never widening an integer to `f64`.\nimpl From<&serde_json::Value> for DslValue {\n    fn from(val: &serde_json::Value) -> Self {\n        match val {\n            serde_json::Value::Null => DslValue::Null,\n            serde_json::Value::Bool(b) => DslValue::Bool(*b),\n            serde_json::Value::Number(n) => {\n                if let Some(v) = n.as_u64().filter(|_| n.is_u64()) {\n                    DslValue::Number(Number::UInt(v))\n                } else if let Some(v) = n.as_i64().filter(|_| n.is_i64()) {\n                    DslValue::Number(Number::Int(v))\n                } else {\n                    DslValue::Number(Number::Float(n.as_f64().unwrap_or(f64::NAN)))\n                }\n            }\n            serde_json::Value::String(s) => DslValue::String(s.clone()),\n            serde_json::Value::Array(items) => DslValue::Array(items.iter().map(DslValue::from).collect()),\n            serde_json::Value::Object(obj) => DslValue::object(obj.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), DslValue::from(v)))),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl From<serde_json::Value> for DslValue {\n    fn from(val: serde_json::Value) -> Self {\n        DslValue::from(&val)\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🌉️ Serializes an owned value through the explicitly exposed Serde boundary.\nimpl serde::Serialize for DslValue {\n    fn serialize<S: serde::Serializer>(&self, serializer: S) -> Result<S::Ok, S::Error> {\n        serde::Serialize::serialize(&serde_json::Value::from(self), serializer)\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🌉️ Deserializes a Serde JSON boundary into an owned value tree.\nimpl<'de> serde::Deserialize<'de> for DslValue {\n    fn deserialize<D: serde::Deserializer<'de>>(deserializer: D) -> Result<Self, D::Error> {\n        serde_json::Value::deserialize(deserializer).map(DslValue::from)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl PartialEq<serde_json::Value> for DslValue {\n    fn eq(&self, other: &serde_json::Value) -> bool {\n        &serde_json::Value::from(self) == other\n    }\n}\n\nimpl PartialEq<DslValue> for serde_json::Value {\n    fn eq(&self, other: &DslValue) -> bool {\n        self == &serde_json::Value::from(other)\n    }\n}\n\n//#region 🔖️Literal\n/// 🧾️ Builds a [`DslValue`] from a JSON-shaped literal — the first-party replacement for\n/// `serde_json::json!` + `DslValue::from` at every action-argument site. Grammar: `null`, `true`,\n/// `false`, `[ … ]`, `{ key: value, … }` (a key is a string literal or any expression convertible\n/// `Into<String>`, e.g. a `const`), and any other expression, converted through [`ToValue`] by method call\n/// (so a borrowed `&String`/`&[T]` auto-derefs to its implementation, as `serde_json::json!` accepts it). Object\n/// entries keep their written order (a `DslValue::Object` is ordered); trailing commas are\n/// accepted. The equivalence law against `serde_json::json!` lives in `🧪️tests/🔬️unit/🦀️.rs`.\n#[macro_export]\nmacro_rules! dsl_value {\n    (@array [$($elements:expr,)*]) => { ::std::vec![$($elements,)*] };\n    (@array [$($elements:expr),*]) => { ::std::vec![$($elements),*] };\n    (@array [$($elements:expr,)*] null $($rest:tt)*) => { $crate::dsl_value!(@array [$($elements,)* $crate::dsl_value!(null)] $($rest)*) };\n    (@array [$($elements:expr,)*] true $($rest:tt)*) => { $crate::dsl_value!(@array [$($elements,)* $crate::dsl_value!(true)] $($rest)*) };\n    (@array [$($elements:expr,)*] false $($rest:tt)*) => { $crate::dsl_value!(@array [$($elements,)* $crate::dsl_value!(false)] $($rest)*) };\n    (@array [$($elements:expr,)*] [$($array:tt)*] $($rest:tt)*) => { $crate::dsl_value!(@array [$($elements,)* $crate::dsl_value!([$($array)*])] $($rest)*) };\n    (@array [$($elements:expr,)*] {$($object:tt)*} $($rest:tt)*) => { $crate::dsl_value!(@array [$($elements,)* $crate::dsl_value!({$($object)*})] $($rest)*) };\n    (@array [$($elements:expr,)*] $next:expr, $($rest:tt)*) => { $crate::dsl_value!(@array [$($elements,)* $crate::dsl_value!($next),] $($rest)*) };\n    (@array [$($elements:expr,)*] $last:expr) => { $crate::dsl_value!(@array [$($elements,)* $crate::dsl_value!($last)]) };\n    (@array [$($elements:expr),*] , $($rest:tt)*) => { $crate::dsl_value!(@array [$($elements,)*] $($rest)*) };\n    (@array [$($elements:expr),*] $unexpected:tt $($rest:tt)*) => { ::std::compile_error!(\"dsl_value!: unexpected token in array\") };\n    (@object $entries:ident () () ()) => {};\n    (@object $entries:ident [$($key:tt)+] ($value:expr) , $($rest:tt)*) => {\n        $entries.push((::std::string::String::from($($key)+), $value));\n        $crate::dsl_value!(@object $entries () ($($rest)*) ($($rest)*));\n    };\n    (@object $entries:ident [$($key:tt)+] ($value:expr) $unexpected:tt $($rest:tt)*) => { ::std::compile_error!(\"dsl_value!: $crate::dsl_value!(@object $entries [$($key)+] ($crate::dsl_value!(false)) $($rest)*); };\n    (@object $entries:ident ($($key:tt)+) (: [$($array:tt)*] $($rest:tt)*) $copy:tt) => { $crate::value::DslValue::Array($crate::dsl_value!(@array [] $($tt)+)) };\n    ({}) => { $crate::value::DslValue::Object(::std::vec::Vec::new()) };\n    ({ $($tt:tt)+ }) => {\n        $crate::value::DslValue::Object({\n            let mut entries: ::std::vec::Vec<(::std::string::String, $crate::value::DslValue)> = ::std::vec::Vec::new();\n            $crate::dsl_value!(@object entries () ($($tt)+) ($($tt)+));\n            entries\n        })\n    };\n    ($other:expr) => {{\n        use $crate::value::ToValue as _;\n        (&$other).to_value()\n    }};\n}\n//#endregion       "source": "\nuse super::*;\n\n#[test]\nfn serde_json_value_round_trips_through_dsl_value() {\n    let original = serde_json::json!({\"name\": \"saw\", \"count\": 3, \"tags\": [\"a\", \"b\"], \"active\": true, \"note\": null});\n    let dsl: DslValue = DslValue::from(&original);\n    let back = serde_json::Value::from(&dsl);\n    assert_eq!(back, original);\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn serde_json_integer_stays_exact_not_widened_to_f64() {\n    let dsl: DslValue = DslValue::from(&serde_json::json!(7));\n    assert_eq!(dsl.as_u64(), Some(7));\n    assert_eq!(dsl.as_f64(), Some(7.0));\n    assert!(matches!(dsl, DslValue::Number(Number::UInt(7))));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn serde_json_negative_integer_becomes_int_variant() {\n    let dsl: DslValue = DslValue::from(&serde_json::json!(-7));\n    assert_eq!(dsl.as_i64(), Some(-7));\n    assert!(matches!(dsl, DslValue::Number(Number::Int(-7))));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn serde_json_float_stays_float_variant() {\n    let dsl: DslValue = DslValue::from(&serde_json::json!(7.5));\n    assert!(matches!(dsl, DslValue::Number(Number::Float(v)) if v == 7.5));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn uint_round_trips_as_bare_integer_text_through_serde_json_value() {\n    let dsl = DslValue::uint(3600);\n    let json = serde_json::Value::from(&dsl);\n    assert_eq!(json.to_string(), \"3600\");\n    assert_eq!(DslValue::from(&json).as_u64(), Some(3600));\n}\n\n#[test]\nfn whole_float_keeps_its_decimal_point_through_serde_json_value() {\n    let dsl = DslValue::float(3600.0);\n    let json = serde_json::Value::from(&dsl);\n    assert_eq!(json.to_string(), \"3600.0\");\n}\n\n/// 🪆️ Object-key-order-insensitive equality — a JSON object's key order carries no semantics,\n/// and `DslValue::Object`'s `Vec`-backed derived `PartialEq` is positional, so a value that\n/// round-tripped through `serde_json`'s (key-sorting) `Map` legitimately comes back with a\n/// different entry order than it started with.       "source": "//! 🧬️ Intrinsic octets have one owned value node and a canonical padded base64 literal.\nuse super::{DslValue,FromValue,ValueError};\n/// 🧬️ Explicit field mapping for an intrinsic octet sequence.\npub fn to_value(bytes:&[u8])->DslValue{DslValue::Bytes(bytes.to_vec())}\n/// 🛫️ Copies octets only after cumulative native output admission.\npub fn to_value_controlled(bytes:&[u8],control:&mut super::NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{control.copy_bytes(bytes).map(DslValue::Bytes).map_err(ValueError::new)}\n/// 🧬️ Accepts owned native octets or their canonical JSON array projection.\npub fn from_value(value:DslValue)->Result<Vec<u8>,ValueError>{match value{DslValue::Bytes(bytes)=>Ok(bytes),value@DslValue::Array(_)=>Vec::<u8>::from_value(value),_=>Err(ValueError::new(\"expected intrinsic octets or their JSON array projection\"))}}\n/// 🛬️ Owns intrinsic octets under the same physical and typed construction budget.\npub fn from_value_controlled(value:&DslValue,control:&mut super::NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Vec<u8>,ValueError>{match value{DslValue::Bytes(bytes)=>control.copy_bytes(bytes).map_err(ValueError::new),DslValue::Array(_)=>Vec::<u8>::from_value_controlled(value,control),_=>Err(ValueError::new(\"expected intrinsic octets or their JSON array projection\"))}}\n/// 🔤️ Uses the single framework-owned standard base64 codec.\npub fn encode_base64(bytes:&[u8])->String{crate::base64_standard_encode(bytes)}\n/// 🔤️ Uses the canonical decoder's strict padding and unused-bit checks.\npub fn decode_base64(text:&str)->Result<Vec<u8>,String>{crate::base64_standard_decode(text).map_err(|error|error.to_string())}\n\n/// 🧬️ Optional intrinsic octets preserve absence independently from an empty sequence.\npub mod optional{\n    use super::*;\n    pub fn to_value(value:&Option<Vec<u8>>)->DslValue{value.as_deref().map_or(DslValue::Null,super::to_value)}\n    /// 🛫️ Admits a present sequence while preserving absent and present-empty states.\n    pub fn to_value_controlled(value:&Option<Vec<u8>>,control:&mut super::super::NativeEncodeControl<'_>)->Result<DslValue,ValueError>{match value{Some(bytes)=>super::to_value_controlled(bytes,control),None=><() as super::super::ToValue>::to_value_controlled(&(),control)}}\n    /// 🛬️ Preserves explicit absence while admitting each present octet copy.\n    pub fn from_value_controlled(value:&DslValue,control:&mut super::super::NativeDecodeControl<'_>)->Result<Option<Vec<u8>>,ValueError>{if value.is_null(){control.step().map_err(ValueError::new)?;Ok(None)}else{super::from_value_controlled(value,control).map(Some)}}\n    pub fn from_value(value:DslValue)->Result<Option<Vec<u8>>,ValueError>{if value.is_null(){Ok(None)}else{super::from_value(value).map(Some)}}\n}\n",

sqlite_snapshot_nested_native_stages_preserve_parent_and_cumulative_ownership(){\n    use std::{cell::Cell,io::Write,process::{Command,Stdio}};\n    fn label(error:&str)->&str{match error{\"native decoding exceeded declared stage workload\"=>\"overrun\",\"native decoding canceled\"=>\"canceled\",\"native decoding ownership exceeds caller limit\"=>\"limit\",\"owned child rejected\"=>\"rejected\",_=>panic!(\"unexpected decode error: {error}\")}}\n    fn run(control:&mut NativeDecodeControl<'_>,operations:&serde_json::Value,errors:&mut Vec<String>)->Result<(),String>{\n        for op in operations.as_array().unwrap(){match op[\"kind\"].as_str().unwrap(){\n            \"begin\"=>control.begin_stage(op[\"units\"].as_u64().unwrap() as usize)?,\n            \"advance\"=>control.advance(op[\"units\"].as_u64().unwrap() as usize)?,\n            \"charge\"=>control.charge(op[\"units\"].as_u64().unwrap() as usize)?,\n            \"reject\"=>return Err(\"owned child rejected\".into()),\n            \"scope\"=>{if let Err(error)=control.scoped_stage(|child|run(child,&op[\"operations\"],errors)){errors.push(label(&error).to_owned());}},\n            kind=>panic!(\"unexpected stage operation: {kind}\")\n        }}Ok(())\n    }\n    let fixture:serde_json::Value=serde_json::from_str(include_str!(\"../🧫️fixtures/🪆️stage/🔣️.json\")).unwrap();\n    let schema:serde_json::Value=serde_json::from_str(include_str!(\"../🧬️schema/🪆️stage/🔣️.json\")).unwrap();\n    let mut actual=Vec::new();\n    for case in fixture[\"cases\"].as_array().unwrap(){\n        let progress=Cell::new(NativeDecodeProgress{completed:0,total:0,owned_bytes:0});\n        let mut callback=|event:NativeDecodeProgress|{progress.set(event);case[\"cancel\"].is_null()||event.total!=case[\"cancel\"][\"total\"].as_u64().unwrap() as usize||event.completed<(case[\"cancel\"][\"at\"].as_u64().unwrap() as usize)};\n        let mut control=NativeDecodeControl::new(case[\"maximumBytes\"].as_u64().unwrap() as usize,&mut callback);let mut errors=Vec::new();\n        if let Err(error)=run(&mut control,&case[\"operations\"],&mut errors){errors.push(label(&error).to_owned());}control.checkpoint().unwrap();\n        let event=progress.get();let result=serde_json::json!({\"progress\":{\"completed\":event.completed,\"total\":event.total,\"ownedBytes\":event.owned_bytes},\"errors\":errors});\n        assert_eq!(result,case[\"expected\"],\"{}\",case[\"id\"]);actual.push(result);\n    }\n    let script=format!(\"{}\\nimport Ajv from 'ajv/dist/2020.js';const input=JSON.parse(await Bun.stdin.text());const ajv=new Ajv({{strict:true}});if(!ajv.validate(input.schema,input.fixture))throw Error('stage fixture');const admit=ajv.getSchema(input.schema.$id+'#/$defs/case');if(input.fixture.cases.some(c=>!admit(c))||input.fixture.refusals.some(c=>admit(c.value)))throw Error('stage admission');await Bun.write(Bun.stdout,JSON.stringify(input.fixture.cases.map(stageOracle)));\",include_str!(\"🪆️stage/🟦️.ts\"));\n    let mut       "source": "//! 📦️ Schema-preserving paged text, sequence, and insertion-ordered map owners.\n\nuse crate::{DslValue, FromValue, ToValue, ValueEdit, ValueError, ValueShape, list::PagedList};\nuse std::fmt::{Debug, Display, Formatter, Write};\n\npub const PAGED_UTF8_CHUNK_BYTES: usize = 1024;\n\nfn append_cold<T, const N: usize>(values: &mut PagedList<T, N>, value: T) -> Result<(), ValueError> {\n    while !values.has_reserved_slot() {\n        let required = values.next_allocation_bytes().map_err(ValueError::new)?;\n        let progress = values.reserve_one(required).map_err(|error| ValueError::new(error.reason))?;\n        if !progress.progressed {\n            return Err(ValueError::new(\"paged owner exact cold allocation did not progress\"));\n        }\n    }\n    values.push_reserved(value).map_err(|_| ValueError::new(\"paged owner rejected its reserved slot\"))\n}\n\nfn paged_index(segment: &str, length: usize) -> Result<usize, ValueError> {\n    if segment.is_empty() || (segment.len() > 1 && segment.starts_with('0')) || !segment.bytes().all(|byte| byte.is_ascii_digit()) {\n        return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"invalid canonical array index `{segment}`\")));\n    }\n    let index = segment.parse::<usize>().map_err(|_| ValueError::new(format!(\"array index `{segment}` is out of range\")))?;\n    (index < length).then_some(index).ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(format!(\"array index `{segment}` is out of range for length {length}\")))\n}\n\n/// 📝️ Arbitrary valid UTF-8 retained as fixed-size, character-boundary-preserving chunks.\npub struct PagedUtf8<const N: usize> {\n    chunks: PagedList<String, N>,\n    byte_len: usize,\n}\n\nimpl<const N: usize> Default for PagedUtf8<N> {\n    fn default() -> Self {\n        Self { chunks: PagedList::default(), byte_len: 0 }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<const N: usize> PagedUtf8<N> {\n    pub fn try_from_str(value: &str) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        if value.len() > N {\n            return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"UTF-8 value has {} bytes, exceeding paged capacity {N}\", value.len())));\n        }\n        let mut output = Self::default();\n        let mut start = 0usize;\n        while start < value.len() {\n            let mut end = (start + PAGED_UTF8_CHUNK_BYTES).min(value.len());\n            while !value.is_char_boundary(end) {\n                end -= 1;\n            }\n            append_cold(&mut output.chunks, value[start..end].to_owned())?;\n            start = end;\n        }\n        output.byte_len = value.len();\n        Ok(output)\n    }\n\n    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {\n        self.byte_len\n    }\n\n    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {\n        self.byte_len == 0\n    }\n\n    pub fn chunks(&self) -> impl DoubleEndedIterator<Item = &str> + ExactSizeIterator {\n        self.chunks.iter().map(String::as_str)\n    }\n\n    pub fn write_to(&self, output: &mut impl Write) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        for chunk in self.chunks() {\n            output.write_str(chunk)?;\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    pub fn to_string_owner(&self) -> String {\n        let mut output = String::with_capacity(self.byte_len);\n        self.write_to(&mut output).expect(\"String formatting is infallible\");\n        output\n    }\n\n    #[doc(hidden)]\n    pub fn retained_chunks(&self) -> &PagedList<String, N> {\n        &self.chunks\n    }\n\n    #[doc(hidden)]\n    pub fn from_retained_chunks(chunks: PagedList<String, N>, byte_len: usize) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        let actual = chunks.iter().try_fold(0usize, |total, chunk| total.checked_add(chunk.len()).ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(\"paged UTF-8 length overflow\")))?;\n        if actual != byte_len || actual > N || chunks.iter().any(|chunk| chunk.len() > PAGED_UTF8_CHUNK_BYTES) {\n            return Err(ValueError::new(\"paged UTF-8 chunks violate their byte or chunk envelope\"));\n        }\n        Ok(Self { chunks, byte_len })\n    }\n\n    #[doc(hidden)]\n    pub fn into_retained_chunks(mut self) -> PagedList<String, N> {\n        std::mem::take(&mut self.chunks)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<const N: usize> Clone for PagedUtf8<N> {\n    fn clone(&self) -> Self {\n        Self { chunks: self.chunks.clone(), byte_len: self.byte_len }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<const N: usize> PartialEq for PagedUtf8<N> {\n    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {\n        self.byte_len == other.byte_len && self.chunks().eq(other.chunks())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<const N: usize> Eq for PagedUtf8<N> {}\n\nimpl<const N: usize> Debug for PagedUtf8<N> {\n    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        formatter.debug_tuple(\"PagedUtf8\").field(&self.to_string_owner()).finish()\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<const N: usize> Display for PagedUtf8<N> {\n    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        self.write_to(formatter)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<const N: usize> ToValue for PagedUtf8<N> {\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        DslValue::String(self.to_string_owner())\n    }\n\n    fn value_at_path(&self, path: &[&str]) -> Result<DslValue, ValueError> {\n        if path.is_empty() { Ok(self.to_value()) } else { Result<(), ValueError> {\n    while !values.has_reserved_slot() {\n        let required = values.next_allocation_bytes().map_err(ValueError::new)?;\n        let progress = values.reserve_one(required).map_err(|error| ValueError::new(error.reason))?;\n        if !progress.progressed {\n            return Err(ValueError::new(\"paged owner exact cold allocation did not progress\"));\n        }\n    }\n    values.push_reserved(value).map_err(|_| ValueError::new(\"paged owner rejected its reserved slot\"))\n}\n\nfn paged_index(segment: &str, length: usize) -> 16;\n\n/// 🗺️ Stores strictly ordered entries in fixed-capacity native pages with resumable directory growth.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct RetainedOrderedMap<K, V> {\n    pages: 16;\n\n/// 🗺️ Stores strictly ordered entries in fixed-capacity native pages with resumable directory growth.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct RetainedOrderedMap<K, V> {\n    pages: from_sorted_entries_for_test(entries: Vec<(K, V)>) -> Result<Self, String>\n    where\n        K: Ord,\n    {\n        if entries.windows(2).any(|pair| pair[0].0 >= pair[1].0) {\n            return entries = entries.into_iter();\n        for _ in 0..page_count {\n            let mut page = Vec::with_capacity(RETAINED_ORDERED_MAP_PAGE_CAPACITY);\n            page.extend(entries.by_ref().take(RETAINED_ORDERED_MAP_PAGE_CAPACITY));\n            pages.push(page);\n        }\n        Ok(Self { pages, len })\n    }\n}\n\nimpl<K: Serialize, V: Serialize>       "source": "//! ♻️ Neutral retained-owner retirement and typed factories.\nuse std::sync::Arc;\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum SnapshotRetirementStep {\n    Pending { released_items: usize, released_bytes: usize },\n    Blocked,\n    Complete,\n}\n\npub trait ErasedSnapshotRetirement: Send {\n    fn close_step(&mut self, maximum_items: usize, maximum_bytes: usize) -> Result<SnapshotRetirementStep, String>;\n    fn terminal_is_empty(&self) -> bool;\n\n    /// 📏️ The SMALLEST byte grant this retirement's next `close_step` can spend to make physical\n    /// progress. A heap allocation is freed whole or not at all, so a retirement whose next unit is\n    /// one owned buffer legitimately answers that buffer's size and answers `Blocked` (or\n    /// `Pending { 0, 0 }`) below it — which leaves a NESTED driver, holding only a\n    /// `Box<dyn ErasedSnapshotRetirement>`, unable to tell \"I under-granted\" from \"I am waiting on\n    /// someone else\". A driver reads this BEFORE it grants, and pays the demand out of its own\n    /// allocation admission rather than out of the caller's payload page.\n    ///\n    /// 🧱️ Defaulted to 1 — the byte-free answer of every retirement that releases owners rather than\n    /// buffers, which is most of them — so no existing implementor changes shape. The inherent\n    /// `next_close_byte_demand` methods that already exist on concrete retirements\n    /// (`🌱️value/🗂️ordered`, `🌊️flow/🧵️retained`) are the same quantity; this is the erased view of\n    /// it, the one a `Box<dyn ErasedSnapshotRetirement>` holder can actually reach.\n    fn next_close_byte_demand(&self) -> usize {\n        1\n    }\n}\n\npub trait SnapshotRetirementFactory<P>: Send + Sync {\n    fn retire(&self, snapshot: Arc<P>) -> Box<dyn ErasedSnapshotRetirement>;\n}\n\npub trait ArtifactOwnedValueRetirementFactory<T>: Send + Sync {\n    fn retire_owned(&self, value: T) -> Box<dyn ErasedSnapshotRetirement>;\n}\n",

A heap allocation is freed whole or not at all, so a retirement whose next unit is\n    /// one owned buffer legitimately answers that buffer's size and answers `Blocked` (or\n    /// `Pending { 0, 0 }`) below it — which leaves a NESTED driver, holding only a\n    /// `Box<dyn ErasedSnapshotRetirement>`, unable to tell \"I under-granted\" from \"I am waiting on\n    /// someone else\". A driver reads this BEFORE it grants, and pays the demand out of its own\n    /// allocation admission rather than out of the caller's payload page.\n    ///\n    /// 🧱️ Defaulted to 1 — the byte-free answer of every retirement that releases owners rather than\n    /// buffers, which is most of them — so no existing implementor changes shape. The inherent\n    /// `next_close_byte_demand` methods that already exist on concrete retirements\n    /// (`🌱️value/🗂️ordered`, `🌊️flow/🧵️retained`) are the same quantity; this is the erased view of\n    /// it, the one a `Box<dyn ErasedSnapshotRetirement>` holder can actually reach.\n    fn next_close_byte_demand(&self) -> usize {\n        1\n    }\n}\n\npub trait SnapshotRetirementFactory<P>: Send + Sync {\n    fn retire(&self, snapshot: Arc<P>) -> Box<dyn ErasedSnapshotRetirement>;\n}\n\npub trait ArtifactOwnedValueRetirementFactory<T>: Send + Sync {\n    fn retire_owned(&self, value: T) -> Box<dyn ErasedSnapshotRetirement>;\n}\n"

parse_quote};\n\nfn field_types(input: &DeriveInput) -> Vec<&Type> {\n    match &input.data {\n        Data::Struct(data) => data.fields.iter().map(|field| &field.ty).collect(),\n        Data::Enum(data) => data.variants.iter().flat_map(|variant| variant.fields.iter().map(|field| &field.ty)).collect(),\n        Data::Union(_) => Vec::new(),\n    }\n}\n\nfn bounded_generics(input: &DeriveInput, bound: TokenStream) -> Generics {\n    let mut generics = input.generics.clone();\n    for ty in field_types(input).into_iter().filter(|ty| !type_mentions_ident(ty, &input.ident)) {\n        generics.make_where_clause().predicates.push(parse_quote!(#ty: #bound));\n    }\n    generics\n}\n\nfn path_arguments_mention(arguments: &PathArguments, ident: &syn::Ident) -> bool {\n    match arguments {\n        PathArguments::None => false,\n        PathArguments::AngleBracketed(arguments) => arguments.args.iter().any(|argument| match argument {\n            GenericArgument::Type(ty) => type_mentions_ident(ty, ident),\n            GenericArgument::AssocType(binding) => type_mentions_ident(&binding.ty, ident),\n            GenericArgument::Constraint(constraint) => constraint.bounds.iter().any(|bound| bound_mentions_ident(bound, ident)),\n            _ => false,\n        }),\n        PathArguments::Parenthesized(arguments) => {\n            arguments.inputs.iter().any(|ty| type_mentions_ident(ty, ident))\n                || match &arguments.output {\n                    ReturnType::Default => false,\n                    ReturnType::Type(_, ty) => type_mentions_ident(ty, ident),\n                }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn bound_mentions_ident(bound: &TypeParamBound, ident: &syn::Ident) -> bool {\n    match bound {\n        TypeParamBound::Trait(bound) => bound.path.segments.iter().any(|segment| segment.ident == *ident || path_arguments_mention(&segment.arguments, ident)),\n        _ => false,\n    }\n}\n\nfn type_mentions_ident(ty: &Type, ident: &syn::Ident) -> bool {\n    match ty {\n        Type::Array(ty) => type_mentions_ident(&ty.elem, ident),\n        Type::BareFn(ty) => {\n            ty.inputs.iter().any(|input| type_mentions_ident(&input.ty, ident))\n                || match &ty.output {\n                    ReturnType::Default => false,\n                    ReturnType::Type(_, output) => type_mentions_ident(output, ident),\n                }\n        }\n        Type::Group(ty) => type_mentions_ident(&ty.elem, ident),\n        Type::ImplTrait(ty) => ty.bounds.iter().any(|bound| bound_mentions_ident(bound, ident)),\n        Type::Paren(ty) => type_mentions_ident(&ty.elem, ident),\n        Type::Path(ty) => ty.qself.as_ref().is_some_and(|qself| type_mentions_ident(&qself.ty, ident)) || ty.path.segments.iter().any(|segment| segment.ident == *ident || path_arguments_mention(&segment.arguments, ident)),\n        Type::Ptr(ty) => type_mentions_ident(&ty.elem, ident),\n        Type::Reference(ty) => type_mentions_ident(&ty.elem, ident),\n        Type::Slice(ty) => type_mentions_ident(&ty.elem, ident),\n        Type::TraitObject(ty) => ty.bounds.iter().any(|bound| bound_mentions_ident(bound, ident)),\n        Type::Tuple(ty) => ty.elems.iter().any(|element| type_mentions_ident(element, ident)),\n        _ => false,\n    }\n}\n\npub fn expand_retire_owned(input: &DeriveInput) -> syn::Result<TokenStream> {\n    let name = &input.ident;\n    let generics = bounded_generics(input, quote!(::semio_framework_value::retirement::RetireOwned));\n    let (impl_generics, ty_generics, where_clause) = generics.split_for_impl();\n    let body = match &input.data {\n        Data::Struct(data) => {\n            let (pattern, values) = destructure_fields(name, &data.fields, None);\n            quote! {\n                let #pattern = self;\n Data::Enum(data) => {\n            let arms = data.variants.iter().map(|variant| {\n                let variant_name = &variant.ident;\n                let (pattern, values) = destructure_fields(name, &variant.fields, Some(variant_name));\n                quote! {\n                    #pattern => ::semio_framework_value::retirement::sequence(vec![\n                        #(::semio_framework_value::retirement::deferred(#values)),*\n                    ])\n                }\n            });\n            quote! { match self { #(#arms),* } }\n        }\n        Data::Union(data) => return Err(syn::Error::new_spanned(data.union_token, \"#[derive(RetireOwned)] does not support unions\")),\n    };\n    Ok(quote! {\n        impl #impl_generics ::semio_framework_value::retirement::RetireOwned for #name #ty_generics #where_clause {\n            fn retirement(self) -> Box<dyn ::semio_framework_value::retirement::RetirementCursor> {\n field)| format_ident!(\"__retained_field_{index}_{}\", field.ident.as_ref().expect(\"named field\"))).collect::<Vec<_>>();\n            let names = named.named.iter().map(|field| field.ident.as_ref().expect(\"named field\"));\n            (quote!(#prefix { #(#names: #values),* }), values)\n        }\n        Fields::Unnamed(unnamed) => {\n            let values = (0..unnamed.unnamed.len()).map(|index| format_ident!(\"__retained_field_{index}\")).collect::<Vec<_>>();\n            (quote!(#prefix ( #(#values),* )), values)\n        }\n        Fields::Unit => (prefix, Vec::new()),\n    }\n}\n\npub fn expand_retained_clone(input: &DeriveInput) -> syn::Result<TokenStream> {\n    match &input.data {\n        Data::Struct(data) => expand_struct(input, No\n/// `#[serde(rename_all = …)]` on the original, so field names stay as declared.\nimpl ToValue for TextError {\n    fn to_value_controlled(&self, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeEncodeControl<'_>) -> Result<DslValue, ValueError> { controlled::encode_text_error(self, c) }\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        let mut entries = vec![(\"message\".to_string(), DslValue::String(self.message.clone())), (\"span\".to_string(), self.span.to_value())];\n        if let Some(expected) = &self.expected {\n            entries.push((\"expected\".to_string(), DslValue::String(expected.clone())));\n        }\n        DslValue::Object(entries)\n    }\n}\nimpl FromValue for TextError {\n    fn from_value_controlled(value: &DslValue, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeDecodeControl<'_>) -> Result<Self, ValueError> { controlled::decode_text_error(value, c) }\n    fn retire_decoded(self) { controlled::retire(self); }\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        let entries = match value {\n            DslValue::Object(entries) => entries,\n            other => return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected an object for TextError, found {other:?}\"))),\n        };\n        let find = |key: &str| entries.iter().find(|(name, _)| name == key).map(|(_, slot)| slot.clone());\n        let message = match find(\"message\") {\n            Some(DslValue::String(text)) => text,\n            other => return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a string for TextError.message, found {other:?}\"))),\n        };\n        let span = match find(\"span\") {\n            Some(slot) => TextSpan::from_value(slot)?,\n            None => return Err(ValueError::new(\"missing TextError.span\")),\n        };\n        let expected = match find(\"expected\") {\n            None | Some(DslValue::Null) => None,\n            Some(DslValue::String(text)) => Some(text),\n            Some(other) => return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a string for TextError.expected, found {other:?}\"))),\n        };\n        Ok(TextError { message, span, expected })\n    }\n}\n\nimpl TextError {\n    pub fn new(message: impl Into<String>, span: TextSpan) -> Self {\n        Self { message: message.into(), span, expected: None }\n    }\n\n    pub fn expected(message: impl Into<String>, span: TextSpan, expected: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        Self { message: message.into(), span, expected: Some(expected.into()) }\n    }\n\n    pub fn from_diagnostic(diagnostic: Diagnostic) -> Self {\n        diagnostic.into_text_error()\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🏷️ Stable dotted fault/diagnostic code (e.g. `module.pack.checksum-mismatch`).\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct FaultCode(pub String);\n\nimpl FaultCode {\n    pub fn new(code: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        Self(code.into())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl From<&'static str> for FaultCode {\n    fn from(value: &'static str) -> Self {\n        Self(value.to_string())\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🌉️ Hand-written, not derived: `FaultCode` is `#[serde(transparent)]`, a shape\n/// `#[derive(ToValue, FromValue)]` does not support (see its own module docstring).\nimpl ToValue for FaultCode {\n    fn to_value_controlled(&self, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeEncodeControl<'_>) -> Result<DslValue, ValueError> { controlled::encode_code(self, c) }\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        DslValue::String(self.0.clone())\n    }\n}\nimpl FromValue for FaultCode {\n    fn from_value_controlled(value: &DslValue, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeDecodeControl<'_>) -> Result<Self, ValueError> { controlled::decode_code(value, c) }\n    fn retire_decoded(self) { controlled::retire(self); }\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        match value {\n            DslValue::String(s) => Ok(FaultCode(s)),\n            other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a string for FaultCode, found {other:?}\"))),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🏷️ Stable, greppable diagnostic identifier, e.g. `\"DSL0001\"`.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct DiagnosticCode(pub &'static str);\n\nimpl From<String> for FaultCode {\n    fn from(value: String) -> Self {\n        Self(value)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl From<DiagnosticCode> for FaultCode {\n    fn from(value: DiagnosticCode) -> Self {\n        FaultCode::new(value.0)\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🚦️ Declaration order is the level order: `#[derive(PartialOrd, Ord)]` makes `Info < Warning <\n/// Error < Fatal` a structural fact, not a hand-maintained comparator. `as_u8`/`from_u8` (0..3)\n/// give a stable wire-compatible numeric mirror for TS/WIT twins.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]\npub enum Severity {\n    Info,\n    Warning,\n    Error,\n    Fatal,\n}\n\n/// 🌉️ Hand-written, not derived: `Severity` is a plain unit-only \"string enum\" (`#[serde(rename_all\n/// = \"camelCase\")]` with no `tag`, serde's default bare-string representation) —\n/// `#[derive(ToValue, FromValue)]`'s enum path only supports internally-tagged representations.\nimpl ToValue for Severity {\n    fn to_value_controlled(&self, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeEncodeControl<'_>) -> Result<DslValue, ValueError> { controlled::encode_severity(self, c) }\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        let name = match self {\n            Severity::Info => \"info\",\n            Severity::Warning => \"warning\",\n            Severity::Error => \"error\",\n            Severity::Fatal => \"fatal\",\n        };\n        DslValue::String(name.to_string())\n    }\n}\nimpl FromValue for Severity {\n    fn from_value_controlled(value: &DslValue, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeDecodeControl<'_>) -> Result<Self, ValueError> { controlled::decode_severity(value, c) }\n    fn retire_decoded(self) { controlled::retire(self); }\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        match value {\n            DslValue::String(s) => match s.as_str() {\n                \"info\" => Ok(Severity::Info),\n                \"warning\" => Ok(Severity::Warning),\n                \"error\" => Ok(Severity::Error),\n                \"fatal\" => Ok(Severity::Fatal),\n                other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"unknown Severity variant `{other}`\"))),\n            },\n            other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a string, found {other:?}\"))),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Severity {\n    /// 🔢️ Stable numeric mirror of declaration order, 0..3.\n    pub fn as_u8(self) -> u8 {\n        match self {\n            Severity::Info => 0,\n            Severity::Warning => 1,\n            Severity::Error => 2,\n            Severity::Fatal => 3,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 🔢️ Inverse of [`as_u8`](Self::as_u8); `None` for any value outside 0..3.\n    pub fn from_u8(value: u8) -> Option<Self> {\n        match value {\n            0 => Some(Severity::Info),\n            1 => Some(Severity::Warning),\n            2 => Some(Severity::Error),\n            3 => Some(Severity::Fatal),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🧭️ What the parser would         "source": "//! ⚠️ Text errors, structured diagnostics, fault reporting, and parse limits.\n// 🚫️async: E1 pure accessor consumed by external-trait impls (serde/Display) — see R9\n\npub use crate::span::TextSpan;\nuse semio_framework_value::{DslValue, FromValue, ToValue, ValueError};\n#[path = \"🎛️controlled/🦀️.rs\"]\npub(crate) mod controlled;\n\n//#region 🔖️Errors\n/// 🚧️ Span-carrying parse/print failure — the one error type every DSL surface returns.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]\npub struct TextError {\n    pub message: String,\n    pub span: TextSpan,\n    pub expected: Option<String>,\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for TextError {\n    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        write!(formatter, \"{} at {}:{}\", self.message, self.span.line, self.span.column)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for TextError {}\n\n/// 🌉️ Hand-written, not derived — same DAG reason as `FaultCode`/`Severity` above. No\n/// `#[serde(rename_all = …)]` on the original, so field names stay as declared.\nimpl ToValue for TextError {\n    fn to_value_controlled(&self, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeEncodeControl<'_>) -> Result<DslValue, ValueError> { controlled::encode_text_error(self, c) }\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        let mut entries = vec![(\"message\".to_string(), DslValue::String(self.message.clone())), (\"span\".to_string(), self.span.to_value())];\n        if let Some(expected) = &self.expected {\n            entries.push((\"expected\".to_string(), DslValue::String(expected.clone())));\n        }\n        DslValue::Object(entries)\n    }\n}\nimpl FromValue for TextError {\n    fn from_value_controlled(value: &DslValue, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeDecodeControl<'_>) -> Result<Self, ValueError> { controlled::decode_text_error(value, c) }\n    fn retire_decoded(self) { controlled::retire(self); }\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        let entries = match value {\n            DslValue::Object(entries) => entries,\n            other => return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected an object for TextError, found {other:?}\"))),\n        };\n        let find = |key: &str| entries.iter().find(|(name, _)| name == key).map(|(_, slot)| slot.clone());\n        let message = match find(\"message\") {\n            Some(DslValue::String(text)) => text,\n            other => return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a string for TextError.message, found {other:?}\"))),\n        };\n        let span = match find(\"span\") {\n            Some(slot) => TextSpan::from_value(slot)?,\n            None => return Err(ValueError::new(\"missing TextError.span\")),\n        };\n        let expected = match find(\"expected\") {\n            None | Some(DslValue::Null) => None,\n            Some(DslValue::String(text)) => Some(text),\n            Some(other) => return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a string for TextError.expected, found {other:?}\"))),\n        };\n        Ok(TextError { message, span, expected })\n    }\n}\n\nimpl TextError {\n    pub fn new(message: impl Into<String>, span: TextSpan) -> Self {\n        Self { message: message.into(), span, expected: None }\n    }\n\n    pub fn expected(message: impl Into<String>, span: TextSpan, expected: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        Self { message: message.into(), span, expected: Some(expected.into()) }\n    }\n\n    pub fn from_diagnostic(diagnostic: Diagnostic) -> Self {\n        diagnostic.into_text_error()\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🏷️ Stable dotted fault/diagnostic code (e.g. `module.pack.checksum-mismatch`).\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct FaultCode(pub String);\n\nimpl FaultCode {\n    pub fn new(code: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        Self(code.into())\n    }\n}\n\nimpl From<&'static str> for FaultCode {\n    fn from(value: &'static str) -> Self {\n        Self(value.to_string())\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🌉️ Hand-written, not derived: `FaultCode` is `#[serde(transparent)]`, a shape\n/// `#[derive(ToValue, FromValue)]` does not support (see its own module docstring).\nimpl ToValue for FaultCode {\n    fn to_value_controlled(&self, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeEncodeControl<'_>) -> Result<DslValue, ValueError> { controlled::encode_code(self, c) }\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        DslValue::String(self.0.clone())\n    }\n}\nimpl FromValue for FaultCode {\n    fn from_value_controlled(value: &DslValue, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeDecodeControl<'_>) -> Result<Self, ValueError> { controlled::decode_code(value, c) }\n    fn retire_decoded(self) { controlled::retire(self); }\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        match value {\n            DslValue::String(s) => Ok(FaultCode(s)),\n            other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a string for FaultCode, found {other:?}\"))),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🏷️ Stable, greppable diagnostic identifier, e.g. `\"DSL0001\"`.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct DiagnosticCode(pub &'static str);\n\nimpl From<String> for FaultCode {\n    fn from(value: String) -> Self {\n        Self(value)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl From<DiagnosticCode> for FaultCode {\n    fn from(value: DiagnosticCode) -> Self {\n        FaultCode::new(value.0)\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🚦️ Declaration order is the level order: `#[derive(PartialOrd, Ord)]` makes `Info < Warning <\n/// Error < Fatal` a structural fact, not a hand-maintained comparator. `as_u8`/`from_u8` (0..3)\n/// give a stable wire-compatible numeric mirror for TS/WIT twins.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]\npub enum Severity {\n    Info,\n    Warning,\n    Error,\n    Fatal,\n}\n\n/// 🌉️ Hand-written, not derived: `Severity` is a plain unit-only \"string enum\" (`#[serde(rename_all\n/// = \"camelCase\")]` with no `tag`, serde's default bare-string representation) —\n/// `#[derive(ToValue, FromValue)]`'s enum path only supports internally-tagged representations.\nimpl ToValue for Severity {\n    fn to_value_controlled(&self, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeEncodeControl<'_>) -> Result<DslValue, ValueError> { controlled::encode_severity(self, c) }\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        let name = match self {\n            Severity::Info => \"info\",\n            Severity::Warning => \"warning\",\n            Severity::Error => \"error\",\n            Severity::Fatal => \"fatal\",\n        };\n        DslValue::String(name.to_string())\n    }\n}\nimpl FromValue for Severity {\n    fn from_value_controlled(value: &DslValue, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeDecodeControl<'_>) -> Result<Self, ValueError> { controlled::decode_severity(value, c) }\n    fn retire_decoded(self) { controlled::retire(self); }\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        match value {\n            DslValue::String(s) => match s.as_str() {\n                \"info\" => Ok(Severity::Info),\n                \"warning\" => Ok(Severity::Warning),\n                \"error\" => Ok(Severity::Error),\n                \"fatal\" => Ok(Severity::Fatal),\n                other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"unknown Severity variant `{other}`\"))),\n            },\n            other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a string, found {other:?}\"))),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Severity {\n    /// 🔢️ Stable numeric mirror of declaration order, 0..3.\n    pub fn as_u8(self) -> u8 {\n        match self {\n            Severity::Info => 0,\n            Severity::Warning => 1,\n            Severity::Error => 2,\n            Severity::Fatal => 3,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// 🔢️ Inverse of [`as_u8`](Self::as_u8); `None` for any value outside 0..3.\n    pub fn from_u8(value: u8) -> Option<Self> {\n        match value {\n            0 => Some(Severity::Info),\n            1 => Some(Severity::Warning),\n            2 => Some(Severity::Error),\n            3 => Some(Severity::Fatal),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🧭️ What the parser would have accepted at the failure point — the raw material for\n/// completions and for `TextError.expected`.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]\npub struct ExpectedSet {\n    pub tokens: Vec<String>,\n    pub keywords: Vec<String>,\n    pub keys: Vec<String>,\n}\n\nimpl ExpectedSet {\n    pub fn describe(&self) -> String {\n        let mut parts = Vec::new();\n        if !self.keywords.is_empty() {\n            parts.push(self.keywords.join(\"|\"));\n        }\n        if !self.keys.is_empty() {\n            parts.push(self.keys.iter().map(|k| format!(\"{k}=\")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(\"|\"));\n        }\n        if !self.tokens.is_empty() {\n            parts.push(self.tokens.join(\"|\"));\n        }\n        parts.join(\" or \")\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🌉️ Hand-written — see `FaultOrigin` above.\nimpl ToValue for ExpectedSet {\n    fn to_value_controlled(&self, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeEncodeControl<'_>) -> Result<DslValue, ValueError> { controlled::encode_expected(self, c) }\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        DslValue::Object(vec![\n            (\"tokens\".to_string(), DslValue::Array(self.tokens.iter().cloned().map(DslValue::String).collect())),\n            (\"keywords\".to_string(), DslValue::Array(self.keywords.iter().cloned().map(DslValue::String).collect())),\n            (\"keys\".to_string(), DslValue::Array(self.keys.iter().cloned().map(DslValue::String).collect())),\n        ])\n    }\n}\nimpl FromValue for ExpectedSet {\n    fn from_value_controlled(value: &DslValue, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeDecodeControl<'_>) -> Result<Self, ValueError> { controlled::decode_expected(value, c) }\n    fn retire_decoded(self) { controlled::retire(self); }\n    fn default_value_controlled(c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeDecodeControl<'_>) -> Result<Self, ValueError> { c.checkpoint().map_err(ValueError::new)?; Ok(Self::default()) }\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        let entries = match value {\n            DslValue::Object(entries) => entries,\n            other => return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected an object for ExpectedSet, found {other:?}\"))),\n        };\n        let strings = |key: &str| -> Result<Vec<String>, ValueError> {\n            match entries.iter().find(|(name, _)| name == key).map(|(_, slot)| slot) {\n                None | Some(DslValue::Null) => Ok(Vec::new()),\n                Some(DslValue::Array(items)) => items\n                    .iter()\n                    .map(|item| match item {\n                        DslValue::String(text) => Ok(text.clone()),\n                        other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a string in ExpectedSet.{key}, found {other:?}\"))),\n                    })\n                    .collect(),\n                Some(other) => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected an array for ExpectedSet.{key}, found {other:?}\"))),\n            }\n        };\n        Ok(ExpectedSet { tokens: strings(\"tokens\")?, keywords: strings(\"keywords\")?, keys: strings(\"keys\")? })\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🩺️ A structured diagnostic anchored to a span, with an optional `ExpectedSet` for\n/// completions/fixes. Lowers into `TextError` at API boundaries that predate diagnostics.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]\npub struct Diagnostic {\n    pub code: FaultCode,\n    pub severity: Severity,\n    pub span: TextSpan,\n    pub message: String,\n    pub expected: Option<ExpectedSet>,\n    pub scope: FaultScope,\n}\n\nimpl Diagnostic {\n    pub fn error(code: &'static str, span: TextSpan, message: impl Into<String>) -> Self {\n        Self { code: FaultCode::new(code), severity: Severity::Error, span, message: message.into(), expected: None, scope: FaultScope::default() }\n    }\n\n    pub fn with_expected(mut self, expected: ExpectedSet) -> Self {\n        self.expected = Some(expected);\n        self\n    }\n\n    pub fn into_text_error(self) -> TextError {\n        let expected = self.expected.as_ref().map(ExpectedSet::describe);\n        match expected {\n            Some(expected) => TextError::expected(self.message, self.span, expected),\n            None => TextError::new(self.message, self.span),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🌉️ Hand-written — see `FaultOrigin` above.\nimpl ToValue for Diagnostic {\n    fn to_value_controlled(&self, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeEncodeControl<'_>) -> Result<DslValue, ValueError> { controlled::encode_diagnostic(self, c) }\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        let mut entries = vec![\n            (\"code\".to_string(), self.code.to_value()),\n            (\"severity\".to_string(), self.severity.to_value()),\n            (\"span\".to_string(), self.span.to_value()),\n            (\"message\".to_string(), DslValue::String(self.message.clone())),\n        ];\n        if let Some(expected) = &self.expected {\n            entries.push((\"expected\".to_string(), expected.to_value()));\n        }\n        entries.push((\"scope\".to_string(), self.scope.to_value()));\n        DslValue::Object(entries)\n    }\n}\nimpl FromValue for Diagnostic {\n    fn from_value_controlled(value: &DslValue, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeDecodeControl<'_>) -> Result<Self, ValueError> { controlled::decode_diagnostic(value, c) }\n    fn retire_decoded(self) { controlled::retire(self); }\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        let entries = match value {\n            DslValue::Object(entries) => entries,\n            other => return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected an object for Diagnostic, found {other:?}\"))),\n        };\n        let find = |key: &str| entries.iter().find(|(name, _)| name == key).map(|(_, slot)| slot.clone());\n        let required = |key: &str| -> Result<DslValue, ValueError> {\n            find(key).ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(format!(\"missing Diagnostic.{key}\")))\n        };\n        let message = match required(\"message\")? {\n            DslValue::String(text) => text,\n            other => return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a string for Diagnostic.message, found {other:?}\"))),\n        };\n        Ok(Diagnostic {\n            code: FaultCode::from_value(required(\"code\")?)?,\n            severity: Severity::from_value(required(\"severity\")?)?,\n            span: TextSpan::from_value(required(\"span\")?)?,\n            message,\n            expected: match find(\"expected\") {\n                None | Some(DslValue::Null) => None,\n                Some(slot) => Some(ExpectedSet::from_value(slot)?),\n            },\n            scope: match find(\"scope\") {\n                None | Some(DslValue::Null) => FaultScope::default(),\n                Some(slot) => FaultScope::from_value(slot)?,\n            },\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n//#region 🔖️Fault\n/// 🧭️ Which layer of the os stack produced a {@link Fault}.\n#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum FaultOrigin {\n    Edge,\n    Renderer,\n    Os,\n    Module,\n    Plugin,\n    App,\n    Extension,\n    /// 🚪️👁️✏️ Ticket 26/08/16/ARTIFACT-VIEWERS-AND-EDITORS-PER-SUBSET contract §2.3: origin for the\n    /// five frozen `surface.*`/`viewer.*` fault codes (`AppRouter`/`OpeningResolver`/`VcsArtifactApp`\n    /// role guard) — additive variant, no existing variant touched, no match site in this crate is\n    /// exhaustive over it (verified with a repo-wide grep before adding).\n    Framework,\n}\n\n/// 🎯️ Optional ids locating a fault/diagnostic to a plugin app surface.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default, PartialEq)]\npub struct FaultScope {\n    pub plugin_id: Option<String>,\n    pub app_id: Option<String>,\n    pub instance_id: Option<String>,\n    pub module: Option<String>,\n    pub body_key: Option<String>,\n}\n\n/// 🔗️ One hop in a {@link Fault} cause chain.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]\npub struct FaultCause {\n    pub message: String,\n    pub code: Option<FaultCode>,\n}\n\n/// 🧯️ Structured abort report crossing every os boundary.\n/// Scope metadata owns a separate allocation to keep error return values compact.\n#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]\npub struct Fault {\n    pub origin: FaultOrigin,\n    pub code: FaultCode,\n    pub severity: Severity,\n    pub message: String,\n    pub scope: Box<FaultScope>,\n    pub span: Option<TextSpan>,\n    pub causes: Vec<FaultCause>,\n    pub retryable: bool,\n}\n\n/// 🌉️ Owned Value conversion preserves the canonical Diagnostic fault wire.\n/// Literal camelCase keys and absent optional fields match the declared fault schema.\nimpl ToValue for FaultOrigin {\n    fn to_value_controlled(&self, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeEncodeControl<'_>) -> Result<DslValue, ValueError> { controlled::encode_origin(self, c) }\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        let name = match self {\n            FaultOrigin::Edge => \"edge\",\n            FaultOrigin::Renderer => \"renderer\",\n            FaultOrigin::Os => \"os\",\n            FaultOrigin::Module => \"module\",\n            FaultOrigin::Plugin => \"plugin\",\n            FaultOrigin::App => \"app\",\n            FaultOrigin::Extension => \"extension\",\n            FaultOrigin::Framework => \"framework\",\n        };\n        DslValue::String(name.to_string())\n    }\n}\nimpl FromValue for FaultOrigin {\n    fn from_value_controlled(value: &DslValue, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeDecodeControl<'_>) -> Result<Self, ValueError> { controlled::decode_origin(value, c) }\n    fn retire_decoded(self) { controlled::retire(self); }\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        match value {\n            DslValue::String(s) => match s.as_str() {\n                \"edge\" => Ok(FaultOrigin::Edge),\n                \"renderer\" => Ok(FaultOrigin::Renderer),\n                \"os\" => Ok(FaultOrigin::Os),\n                \"module\" => Ok(FaultOrigin::Module),\n                \"plugin\" => Ok(FaultOrigin::Plugin),\n                \"app\" => Ok(FaultOrigin::App),\n                \"extension\" => Ok(FaultOrigin::Extension),\n                \"framework\" => Ok(FaultOrigin::Framework),\n                other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"unknown FaultOrigin variant `{other}`\"))),\n            },\n            other => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a string, found {other:?}\"))),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🌉️ Hand-written — see `FaultOrigin` above.\nimpl ToValue for FaultScope {\n    fn to_value_controlled(&self, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeEncodeControl<'_>) -> Result<DslValue, ValueError> { controlled::encode_scope(self, c) }\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        let mut entries: Vec<(String, DslValue)> = Vec::new();\n        for (key, slot) in [\n            (\"pluginId\", &self.plugin_id),\n            (\"appId\", &self.app_id),\n            (\"instanceId\", &self.instance_id),\n            (\"module\", &self.module),\n            (\"bodyKey\", &self.body_key),\n        ] {\n            if let Some(text) = slot {\n                entries.push((key.to_string(), DslValue::String(text.clone())));\n            }\n        }\n        DslValue::Object(entries)\n    }\n}\nimpl FromValue for FaultScope {\n    fn from_value_controlled(value: &DslValue, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeDecodeControl<'_>) -> Result<Self, ValueError> { controlled::decode_scope(value, c) }\n    fn retire_decoded(self) { controlled::retire(self); }\n    fn default_value_controlled(c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeDecodeControl<'_>) -> Result<Self, ValueError> { c.checkpoint().map_err(ValueError::new)?; Ok(Self::default()) }\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        let entries = match value {\n            DslValue::Object(entries) => entries,\n            other => return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected an object for FaultScope, found {other:?}\"))),\n        };\n        let take = |key: &str| -> Result<Option<String>, ValueError> {\n            match entries.iter().find(|(name, _)| name == key).map(|(_, slot)| slot) {\n                None | Some(DslValue::Null) => Ok(None),\n                Some(DslValue::String(text)) => Ok(Some(text.clone())),\n                Some(other) => Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a string for FaultScope.{key}, found {other:?}\"))),\n            }\n        };\n        Ok(FaultScope {\n            plugin_id: take(\"pluginId\")?,\n            app_id: take(\"appId\")?,\n            instance_id: take(\"instanceId\")?,\n            module: take(\"module\")?,\n            body_key: take(\"bodyKey\")?,\n        })\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🌉️ Hand-written — see `FaultOrigin` above.\nimpl ToValue for FaultCause {\n    fn to_value_controlled(&self, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeEncodeControl<'_>) -> Result<DslValue, ValueError> { controlled::encode_cause(self, c) }\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        let mut entries = vec![(\"message\".to_string(), DslValue::String(self.message.clone()))];\n        if let Some(code) = &self.code {\n            entries.push((\"code\".to_string(), code.to_value()));\n        }\n        DslValue::Object(entries)\n    }\n}\nimpl FromValue for FaultCause {\n    fn from_value_controlled(value: &DslValue, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeDecodeControl<'_>) -> Result<Self, ValueError> { controlled::decode_cause(value, c) }\n    fn retire_decoded(self) { controlled::retire(self); }\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        let entries = match value {\n            DslValue::Object(entries) => entries,\n            other => return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected an object for FaultCause, found {other:?}\"))),\n        };\n        let find = |key: &str| entries.iter().find(|(name, _)| name == key).map(|(_, slot)| slot.clone());\n        let message = match find(\"message\") {\n            Some(DslValue::String(text)) => text,\n            other => return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a string for FaultCause.message, found {other:?}\"))),\n        };\n        let code = match find(\"code\") {\n            None | Some(DslValue::Null) => None,\n            Some(slot) => Some(FaultCode::from_value(slot)?),\n        };\n        Ok(FaultCause { message, code })\n    }\n}\n\n/// 🌉️ Hand-written — see `FaultOrigin` above.\nimpl ToValue for Fault {\n    fn to_value_controlled(&self, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeEncodeControl<'_>) -> Result<DslValue, ValueError> { controlled::encode_fault(self, c) }\n    fn to_value(&self) -> DslValue {\n        let mut entries = vec![\n            (\"origin\".to_string(), self.origin.to_value()),\n            (\"code\".to_string(), self.code.to_value()),\n            (\"severity\".to_string(), self.severity.to_value()),\n            (\"message\".to_string(), DslValue::String(self.message.clone())),\n            (\"scope\".to_string(), self.scope.to_value()),\n        ];\n        if let Some(span) = &self.span {\n            entries.push((\"span\".to_string(), span.to_value()));\n        }\n        if !self.causes.is_empty() {\n            entries.push((\"causes\".to_string(), DslValue::Array(self.causes.iter().map(ToValue::to_value).collect())));\n        }\n        entries.push((\"retryable\".to_string(), DslValue::Bool(self.retryable)));\n        DslValue::Object(entries)\n    }\n}\nimpl FromValue for Fault {\n    fn from_value_controlled(value: &DslValue, c: &mut semio_framework_value::NativeDecodeControl<'_>) -> Result<Self, ValueError> { controlled::decode_fault(value, c) }\n    fn retire_decoded(self) { controlled::retire(self); }\n    fn from_value(value: DslValue) -> Result<Self, ValueError> {\n        let entries = match value {\n            DslValue::Object(entries) => entries,\n            other => return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected an object for Fault, found {other:?}\"))),\n        };\n        let find = |key: &str| entries.iter().find(|(name, _)| name == key).map(|(_, slot)| slot.clone());\n        let required = |key: &str| -> Result<DslValue, ValueError> {\n            find(key).ok_or_else(|| ValueError::new(format!(\"missing Fault.{key}\")))\n        };\n        let message = match required(\"message\")? {\n            DslValue::String(text) => text,\n            other => return Err(ValueError::new(format!(\"expected a string for Fault.message, found {other:?}\"))),\n        };\n        Ok(Fault {\n            origin: FaultOrigin::from_value(required(\"origin\")?)?,\n            code: FaultCode::from_value(required(\"code\")?)?,\n            severity: Severity::from_value(required(\"severity\")?)?,\n            message,\n            scope: Box::new(match find(\"scope\") {\n                None | Some(DslValue::Null) => FaultScope::default(),\n                Some(slot) => FaultScope::from_value(slot)?,\n            }),\n            span: match find(\"span\") {\n                None | Some(DslValue::Null) => None,\n
